summary: Dan Wakeford, founder of Celebrity Intelligence, told Fox News Digital the heir to the British throne is approaching royal duty in a different way
story: Dan Wakeford, founder of Celebrity Intelligence, says Prince Williams' strategic approach to work, family and privacy is helping modernize the monarchy while boosting public support.
Prince William has been branded "work-shy" for years, but one royal expert says the heir to the British throne is quietly executing a CEO-style strategy designed to secure the monarchy's future.

Dan Wakeford, founder of Celebrity Intelligence, told Fox News Digital that the father of three isn't fazed by critics as he continues to prioritize his family while placing less emphasis on tradition and more on key engagements aimed at strengthening the institution.

"William is extremely good at setting boundaries and not working during the holidays, protecting his kids’ privacy and his wife’s mental health," said Wakeford. "There’s some criticism of that. Some critics snipe at that and think that he’s ‘work-shy’ or a little bit lazy. But I think William is working more like a CEO and being very strategic with his time."
KATE MIDDLETON IS 'INDISPENSABLE' TO ROYAL FAMILY AS SLIMMED-DOWN MONARCHY FACES MOUNTING PRESSURE: EXPERT

Prince William, Prince of Wales, known as the Duke of Rothesay and Catherine, Princess of Wales, known as the Duchess of Rothesay when in Scotland, smile to well-wishers as they arrive for a visit to Aros Hall, a local community hub on April 29, 2025, in Tobermory, Scotland. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

"He studies the monarchy in a way to help make it survive and keeps a boundary around his real life and his relationships so that he doesn’t get burned out, and he can do the best job possible," Wakeford shared. "And the poll numbers show that he’s extremely popular, and he’s doing a good job."

The royal family’s working ranks have grown increasingly slimmed down in recent years. In 2019, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor stepped back from public duties following a disastrous televised interview in which he attempted to explain his friendship with late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. He lost his title of prince and other honors in 2025.

The former Prince Andrew (left) and his nephew Prince William attend Katharine, Duchess of Kent's requiem mass service at Westminster Cathedral on Sept. 16, 2025, in London. William and his wife Catherine have been "deeply concerned" by the latest revelations linking Andrew to late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, Kensington Palace said on Feb. 9, 2026. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

In 2020, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, made their exit as working royals and moved to California. While King Charles has maintained a full schedule, he continues to undergo cancer treatment.

Catherine Mayer, author of "Divide & Rule," previously told People magazine that the senior royals "are all stretched thin — and none of them are young," adding that "William and Catherine carry the whole thing."
"William is the very antithesis of 'work-shy,'" Christopher Andersen, author of "Kate!" told Fox News Digital.

Prince William, Prince of Wales, known as the Duke of Cornwall when in Cornwall, greets members of the public at Helston Community Fire Station during a visit to Cornwall for St. Piran's Day on March 5, 2026, in Helston, England. (Aaron Chown-WPA Pool/Getty Images)
"The Prince and Princess of Wales want to make a real impact by raising awareness of mental health, cancer research and other causes they're prioritizing," Andersen said.

"Does William want to be the first king to run the monarchy like a CEO? Well, it's been called 'The Firm' for decades, hasn't it? The royal family is worth billions, including extensive prime real estate holdings. To say it should be taken seriously as a business enterprise is a colossal understatement."

HRH Prince William, the Prince of Wales, sits with his children Prince George and Princess Charlotte in the Royal Box during the Wimbledon Lawn Tennis Championships on July 12, 2026, in London. (Tim Clayton/Getty Images)

William has long-faced criticism for taking on fewer engagements than other senior royals, earning the "work-shy" label. Last year, The Sunday Times reported that Princess Anne wanted her nephew to take on more "bread-and-butter" engagements as he prepares for the throne, citing unnamed sources close to the princess. Fox News Digital reached out to Buckingham Palace for comment at the time.

Journalist Emily Andrews previously reported that William once confronted her about an article she wrote titled "Work Shy Wills." According to Andrews, William told her there were "a lot of things we hadn't seen behind the scenes."

Britain's Prince William, Prince of Wales, and Princess Anne, Princess Royal, leave St. George's Chapel during the annual Order of the Garter Service at Windsor Castle on June 15, 2026, in Windsor. (Toby Shepheard - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"Princess Anne will always do more engagements," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "That’s her job. But William has the monarch’s permission to prioritize his young family. And in 2026, that stability is part of the job.

"Preparing to run the monarchy like a CEO doesn’t mean less work. It means different work. Forget 400 meet-and-greets. We’re getting 10-year projects. We’re talking about big goals, big partnerships and measurable, real outcomes."
Catherine, Princess of Wales and Prince William of Wales attend Commonwealth Day celebrations at Westminster Abbey in London, on March 10, 2025. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"King Charles is like the custodian," Chard continued. "His mission is to preserve and consider a slimmed-down monarchy. Prince William, the strategist, is making the monarchy indispensable for the next 50 years. The traditional charity work is not going anywhere. Charities still need royal visits to raise money and profile. However, there will be more efficient, targeted visits."
Prince William, Prince of Wales, attends Day 14 of the Wimbledon Tennis Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in London, on July 12, 2026. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
Wakeford noted that William's workload cannot be judged solely by the number of public appearances he makes.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Prince William, Prince of Wales, smiles as he rides in a boat during a tour of the Guapimirim mangrove area in Guanabara Bay, managed by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation, on Nov. 4, 2025, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Aaron Chown-Pool/Getty Images)

The royal family's website says the Prince of Wales carries out official duties in support of the king while overseeing charitable projects in Britain and abroad. He leads long-term initiatives, including Homewards and the Earthshot Prize. He's also responsible for leading the Duchy of Cornwall.
The Times also reported that William plans to sell about 20% of the Duchy of Cornwall's estate over the next decade to help fund housing, environmental and renewable energy projects.

Prince William, Prince of Wales, known as the Duke of Rothesay when in Scotland, and King Charles III attend the Thistle Service at St. Giles' Cathedral on July 1, 2026, in Edinburgh, Scotland. (Aaron Chown - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

"A major part of his duty is to raise a future king," British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "His focus on being a good father to Prince George is critically important. Prince William and his family present a strong visual image, which is a significant asset in the age of social media."
"Princess Catherine is by his side, emphasizing family stability. Their appeal lies not so much in the volume of events but in making the monarchy more modern and stable."

Catherine, Princess of Wales and Prince William view exhibits from the Royal Collection in the Green Drawing Room during German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's state visit to Britain on Dec. 3, 2025, in Windsor, England. (Aaron Chown-Pool/Getty Images)
Some royal experts have cautioned that if the monarchy becomes too focused on metrics, branding and management, it could risk losing the mystique and tradition that make it unique.
"The question needs to be asked: Does Britain want a royal family run like a business?" royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital.
Prince William, Prince of Wales, takes part in a panel discussion during Earthshot+ at Portside Tower on Nov. 5, 2024, in Cape Town, South Africa. (Phil Noble - Pool/Getty Images)

"Why should William wish to change the principles of royalty devised over 800 years? The view I come back to constantly is that the royal family should never forget. It is the blood, sweat and tears of the British taxpayers who finance the royal family. Although King Charles understands this, the jury is out on William. The lazy label attached to William in the past may have spurred him into action. But his alleged new style for the future could change many things."

Prince William, Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales are seen here at the DMMI Royal Charity Polo Cup 2026 in Windsor, England, on July 10, 2026. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
William's reported plans to modernize the monarchy won't spell the end of royal pomp and pageantry, Andersen argued.

Prince William is heir to the British throne. (Aaron Chown - Pool/Getty Images)

"William and Kate are both keenly aware of how important it is to keep up appearances and centuries-old traditions," he said. "No matter how business-savvy William is as king, or how smoothly the monarchy runs, the public probably won’t see it. What they’ll see, what the royal family wants them to see, is the familiar, magical fairy tale."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Halle Berry sizzles in racy lingerie look for sunset beach stroll during Fiji getaway
summary: Halle Berry shared stunning Fiji vacation photos in a gold bikini and animal-print cover-up as she prepares to celebrate her 60th birthday soon.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Halle Berry is enjoying a tropical reset ahead of her 60th birthday.
The 59-year-old actress shared a series of Instagram photos from a tropical getaway in Fiji, offering glimpses of quiet mornings, poolside relaxation and sunset walks along the beach.
Berry posed near the shoreline in an animal-print cover-up layered over a black lace lingerie bodysuit as the sun dipped toward the ocean.
The flowing black-and-white wrap featured wide sleeves and tassel detailing, while her short, tousled hair blew across her face as she smiled for the camera.
KRISTIN CAVALLARI FLAUNTS HER TONED FIGURE IN BIKINIS DURING EUROPEAN SUMMER VACATION
Halle Berry shared sizzling photos from her Fiji vacation. (Stephanie Cardinale/Getty Images)
"The only bad thing about this trip is that each day must come to an end," she captioned the post.

A separate Instagram post captured the Academy Award winner in silhouette beneath sheer fabric draped around an outdoor daybed. Berry arched backward as the setting sun streamed through the material, with palm trees, an infinity pool and the ocean visible beyond the shaded retreat.
Halle Berry shared a peaceful sunset moment from her tropical getaway in Fiji. (Halle Berry/Instagram)

In a separate poolside image, the "Catwoman" star reclined along the edge of the water in a gold bikini. A wide-brimmed straw hat rested across her torso as she stretched one arm across the wooden deck and displayed several rings and stacked bracelets.
Halle Berry embraced the relaxed pace of island life during her Fiji vacation. (Halle Berry/Instagram)

Berry also shared an artful reflection photographed through a glass window. The layered image showed the actress appearing to relax inside a rounded bathtub while the surrounding ocean, palm trees and outdoor pool reflected across the glass.
GISELE BÜNDCHEN CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY IN LEOPARD-PRINT BIKINI AS SHE REFLECTS ON GRATITUDE
Berry turns 60 Aug. 14 (Getty Images)
Halle Berry relaxed with an oceanfront soak during her Fiji getaway. (Halle Berry/Instagram)
The actress appeared to be enjoying the laid-back pace of the trip, joking in another caption, "We got drunk last night, and still drunk today 🤪."
Berry’s vacation comes as she prepares to celebrate her 60th birthday and continues challenging expectations about how women should approach aging.
During a July appearance on Hoda Kotb’s "Making Space" podcast, Berry said the milestone feels far different than she once imagined.

"I’m so happy to still be here, you know. When I was growing up and I thought of 60, it felt so old, you know. And now that I am 60, um, it doesn’t feel old at all," she said. "You know, I’m like, this is 60. Well, that’s not so bad."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Halle Berry recently reflected on aging and embracing her next chapter ahead of her 60th birthday. (Mike Marsland/WireImage/Getty Images)
Berry said she feels more comfortable and confident in herself than she has in years.
"I feel really great actually. If I’m honest, I feel, I think, better than I have in a very, very long time," she said. "Um, I feel more of myself. I feel all of myself."
The Oscar winner explained that growing older has allowed her to stop worrying about satisfying everyone else’s expectations.

"You do stop managing everybody’s expectations," Berry told Kotb. "You do start to realize you’re usually the oldest person in the room. And, so, with that, you know, that carries some weight. You get to do what you wanna do.
'KNOTS LANDING' ICON DONNA MILLS JOINS ONLYFANS AT 85 TO CONNECT WITH FANS 'ON HER OWN TERMS’
"You get to be who you wanna be, say what you want to say. You know, you’re no longer walking on eggshells, and that’s a really wonderful place to arrive."
Berry also pushed back against the idea that reaching a certain age should mean stepping away from her career permanently.
The actress said people have asked whether she intends to continue making movies before suggesting she has already accomplished enough.
"'Are you still going to keep working in movies?'" Berry recalled being asked. "And I say, ‘Yeah, why should I not?’"
She said others have questioned whether it is time for her to "quit all that and sit down somewhere and just be on a permanent vacation."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Berry rejected the assumption that women should withdraw from professional life as they grow older, arguing that meaningful work continues to provide purpose and connection.

"Why do I wanna? After I’ve worked my whole life so hard and it’s made me feel all of myself, it’s validated who I was, it’s, it’s given me a sense of purpose," she said. "Why should I now sit down and give that all away? And then what?"
The actress said she encourages her 18-year-old daughter, Nahla, to pursue work she genuinely loves so that retirement never feels like the ultimate goal.
"Choose what you love so that you never feel like you want to retire because working and being active and contributing is what keeps us young as we go down the path of life," Berry said.
"It keeps us connected to life, to ourselves, to the others. You, you never want to stop doing that thing that you love so much."

title: Diddy's federal prison release delayed weeks after reported solitary confinement stint
summary: Sean Diddy Combs' federal prison release date was pushed back to Feb. 20, 2028, after he was reportedly sent to solitary confinement after a prison fight.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Sean "Diddy" Combs' federal prison release date has changed once again.
Diddy, 56, is now expected to leave prison Feb. 20, 2028, nearly one month after his previously scheduled release date, according to the Federal Bureau of Prisons.
Diddy's release date has changed multiple times since he began serving his sentence.
According to multiple reports, the disgraced rap mogul was reportedly sent to solitary confinement last month after a prison fight with another inmate.
DIDDY SENT TO SOLITARY CONFINEMENT AFTER PRISON FIGHT WITH ANOTHER INMATE: MULTIPLE REPORTS

The Federal Bureau of Prisons moved Sean "Diddy" Combs' release date back after a reported incident at the FCI Fort Dix prison. It's unclear if his release date was delayed due to the reported fight. (Scott Dudelson)
The incident began after a fellow inmate "made a remark to Combs, which instigated the event" at FCI Fort Dix, ABC News reported at the time.
Diddy was then reportedly sent to solitary confinement, the outlet noted. It's unclear if his release date was delayed due to the reported fight.
CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

"For privacy, safety and security reasons, we do not release information regarding the conditions of confinement for any inmate, including housing assignments, nor do we discuss whether a particular inmate is the subject of allegations, investigations or sanctions," a representative for the Federal Bureau of Prisons told Fox News Digital.
Sean "Diddy" Combs did not testify in his federal trial for sex crimes. (Stephen Lovekin/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Diddy's representatives declined Fox News Digital's request for comment.

In September 2024, the "Last Night" singer was arrested on federal sex trafficking charges after months of sexual misconduct allegations, lawsuits, investigations and the release of surveillance video that appeared to show the rapper severely beating then-girlfriend Cassie in the hallway of a Los Angeles hotel.
He was sentenced to more than four years behind bars in October after being convicted in July on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution.

Cassie and Diddy met in 2006 and officially ended their romantic relationship in 2018. (Getty Images)
Cassie, who was pregnant with her third child, testified over the course of four days in the Diddy trial last summer. (Jane Rosenberg)
Diddy initially faced a maximum of life in prison if convicted on charges that included racketeering conspiracy, sex trafficking by force, coercion and transportation to engage in prostitution.

A jury convicted Diddy on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution July 2, 2025. The "I'll Be Missing You" rapper was acquitted of the most serious charges of racketeering and sex trafficking.

In addition to the 50-month sentence, Diddy was ordered to serve five years of supervised release and pay a $500,000 fine. The prosecution recommended 135 months (just over 11 years) for his sentencing.

title: Martha Stewart gets candid about plastic surgery, dating as she turns 85
summary: Martha Stewart shared a hot tub photo from her Maine estate on her 85th birthday and revealed to People magazine she has never had plastic surgery.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Martha Stewart isn't planning to go under the knife or settle down with an older partner.
The lifestyle icon is embracing turning 85 on her own terms, opening up about plastic surgery, dating and aging in a new interview as she celebrated the milestone birthday.
Stewart doubled down on her long-held approach to aging naturally, revealing she has never undergone plastic surgery despite decades in the public eye.
Martha Stewart recently reflected on aging, dating and her approach to plastic surgery. (Jose Perez/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images/Getty Images)
JANE SEYMOUR, 75, SHARES HOW SHE APPROACHES AGING WITH VITALITY: 'BEST I CAN BE'
"I have not had any plastic surgery at all. I don't think I need it," Stewart told People magazine.
Instead, Stewart said she relies on consistent skin care, facial treatments and healthy habits to maintain her appearance.
"I use a little bit of fillers," she explained. "I go maybe once every four months for touch-ups.
"I'm more a maintenance kind of person. I'm not getting boobs done and hips and butts and stuff like that."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Martha Stewart is shown earlier in her career alongside a photo from a recent public appearance. (CBS via Getty Images; Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for Telemundo/Getty Images)
Stewart also opened up about her outlook on relationships later in life, saying companionship has become less important as she's gotten older.
"Now, it's less important," she said when asked whether she still envies friends with happy marriages. "The older you get, the less you really need a mate, I think.
"I wouldn't want to be beleaguered with an older, ill person."
Stewart also marked her 85th birthday by sharing a photo of herself relaxing in a bubbling hot tub during a stay in Maine.

She appeared to be unwinding at her sprawling Maine estate, where she soaked in the steaming water while wearing a black swimsuit. Evergreen trees surrounded the tranquil setting, with a sprawling pool stretching out behind the hot tub.
'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS SAYS SHE WON'T 'BE QUIET' AFTER CRITIC TARGETED HER MAKEUP AT AGE 85
Martha Stewart has made several public appearances recently. (Getty Images for Dom PÃ©rignon)
"I am going to use this amazing hot tub every single day I am in maine," Stewart wrote alongside the photo. "Invigorating restorative Therapeutic relaxing."
Fans quickly flooded the comments with compliments, with one writing, "Damn serving face too," while another added, "Martha you are everything truly."
The birthday milestone comes as Stewart continues embracing getting older on her own terms.
"I don't think about age," she told People. "Eighty-five is just a number; that's all I consider it. I don't want to have a party. It's not a big deal.
"My goal is to keep learning about everything."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
Stewart credited much of her youthful appearance to the lifestyle she has maintained for decades.
"I have good genes. My mom looked great at 95," she said. "We eat well. We don't drink very much. We don't smoke. We eat healthy food. We exercise daily. I horseback-ride."
Stewart's disciplined routine extends well beyond her diet. She told People she still wakes at 3 a.m. every morning to complete her daily puzzles before starting her day.
Turning 85 hasn't slowed Stewart down.

The lifestyle entrepreneur recently recreated her 1995 People cover at her 156-acre Bedford, New York, farm, where she reflected on the career that made her the country's best-known homemaking authority.
ROSIE O'DONNELL WALKED AWAY AT THE HEIGHT OF HER SUCCESS AFTER REACHING ONE JAW-DROPPING FINANCIAL MILESTONE
Martha Stewart has called herself a "perfectionist." (Valerie Terranova/Getty Images)

"I still am a perfectionist. I still like to do many things at the same time. I like to do all the same things I've pretty much always done," Stewart said. "I'd like to have a little bit more free time. I don't have any free time at all, but I'm working on that."

Raised in Nutley, New Jersey, Stewart began modeling before launching a catering business and publishing her first cookbook, "Entertaining," helping build an empire that expanded into magazines, television, retail partnerships and home products. She became the first self-made female billionaire in the United States in 1999.

She has since authored more than 100 cookbooks, opened restaurants, become the oldest Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model at age 81 and continues adding new ventures to her résumé, including her home intelligence app Hint, a skin care line and multiple brand partnerships.
Asked whether she already has everything she wants, Stewart pointed to her newest venture.
"No, I don't. I didn't have an app for my home, and so I'm making one," she said.

title: Former Disney star Bella Thorne says cruel accusations after nude photo blackmail attempt 'really broke me'
summary: Bella Thorne revealed on "Call Her Daddy" how the FBI traced her alleged hacker's identity through the screenshots she posted on social media.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Bella Thorne fought back against an alleged blackmailer by releasing her own nude photos in 2019. But the former Disney star said it was the flood of victim-blaming accusations that "really, really broke" her.

The former Disney Channel star found herself at the center of a headline-making scandal when she accused a hacker of attempting to blackmail her with private nude photos. Thorne ultimately beat the alleged extortionist to the punch by releasing the images herself.
"I just did an honest Twitter post," Thorne recalled during an appearance on "Call Her Daddy." "I just kind of set it out as ... you're not gonna keep taking this from me, so here it is."
FORMER DISNEY STAR BELLA THORNE STUNS IN GREEN SEQUIN BIKINI DURING BEACH DAY WITH FIANCÉ

Bella Thorne said the public backlash following her 2019 nude photo blackmail ordeal "really, really broke me" during an appearance on the "Call Her Daddy" podcast. (Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images)

Thorne said she shared the images to take control of the situation before the alleged blackmailer could release them. The decision sparked a wave of backlash that the "Shake It Up" star said left her emotionally devastated.

"And you know, I think the worst part of that was people saying, 'Well, you did this. You are faking it. You just wanna show us your t---. You want us so badly to see your private parts that that's why you're doing it. You want it.' And that, to me, like, really broke me then. That like, really, really broke me," Thorne told host Alexandra Cooper.
The 28-year-old actress recalled filming an Instagram story in which she was "completely ... broken and so upset, just mad."
Bella Thorne rose to fame as CeCe Jones on the Disney Channel hit series "Shake It Up," starring alongside Zendaya from 2010 to 2013. (Bob D'Amico/Disney Channel)
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
The ordeal eventually took an unexpected turn when Thorne said she received a call from the FBI.

"And then I get like a call one day, and it's the FBI. And they're like, 'Hey, you know, we've seen this thing. We think it's our guy and, like, can we come over? Can we get all the data? Can we see what this is?' And they came over to my house," Thorne recalled. "So, now I have like a house full of FBI, which is like the craziest thing."
Bella Thorne said she later worked with the FBI for more than a year after investigators contacted her about the alleged blackmail case. (Gary Miller/Getty Images for Glass House Brands)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Bella Thorne said the screenshots she shared with investigators ultimately helped authorities identify the alleged suspect. (Alberto Rodriguez/Penske Media)
Thorne said she worked closely with the FBI for more than a year, sharing all the information she had. She said investigators ultimately identified the suspect by matching his writing style.
"So, if I had not posted those screenshots ... they wouldn't have caught him," she said. "Or maybe they would've caught him later, but they wouldn't have had that direct source."
She said sharing the screenshots ultimately helped investigators build their case.
"And that's how they knew is because of the screenshots," Thorne added. "Because it's his exact writing, and they're like, 'This is his MO. It's the same guy, it has to be.'"

title: Miranda Kerr's ultra-specific diet includes venison for breakfast, no eggs or seed oils
summary: Miranda Kerr revealed her strict diet, including venison for breakfast, no eggs and zero seed oils or dairy. She said eating better has helped her feel better.
story: Health and wellness expert Jillian Michaels warns against the viral healthmaxxing trend and the danger of 'health FOMO' on social media. She criticizes young women for taking health advice from influencers who 'don't know what they're talking about,' contrasting them with medically trained doctors.
Miranda Kerr recently detailed her ultra healthy, if a bit unique, diet, which includes eating venison for breakfast and cutting out eggs altogether.

"I love food, but when I got sick, I had to learn even more that food is medicine," the former Victoria’s Secret Angel told Kristin Cavallari on her "Let’s be Honest" podcast. "So, I love to have nutritious and delicious foods that feed my soul, but, at the same time, I don’t crave like unhealthy food anymore because I know how detrimental that can be to my body on the inside, not even about what it looks like on the outside, but on the inside.
"I want to have vitality and energy and that’s kind of why I eat healthy."
Two years ago, Kerr revealed she was diagnosed with proctitis, a form of irritable bowl syndrome, when she was pregnant with her second son six years earlier.
MIRANDA KERR RECALLS FIRST MEETING EX ORLANDO BLOOM'S FIANCEE KATY PERRY: 'WE JUST IMMEDIATELY GOT ALONG'
Miranda Kerr has an unusual diet. (Getty Images)
She told Get the Gloss at the time she drank a liter of celery juice a day, which is known to be an anti-inflammatory, and said she is now in remission.
The 43-year-old supermodel told Cavallari she wants to be able to run around with her grandkids someday, "be baking them cakes like my grandma did for me" and feel healthy "for as long as" she can.

"‘Cause I think that’s more important than what you look like," she argued. "It’s so much more important that you feel that vitality, and that’s why I say that my non-negotiables are meditation. Like, I’m doing that instead of working out, I guess you could say, with the busy life that I have right now, but that’s the choice that I make because that’s what feeds me."
She said other people might be "really fed" by going for a run in the morning, for example.
"Each to their own. You have to find what elevates you, what de-stresses you," she said.
She also loves dance parties with her kids.
Kerr shares Flynn, 15, with ex-husband Orlando Bloom and Hart, 8, Myles, 6, and Pierre, 2, with her husband, Snapchat founder Evan Spiegel.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
She said she’s been drinking Noni juice, which she calls a "superfood superfruit," in the morning for 30 years since she was 13.
"What I love about it is it’s full of antioxidants, and it has a lot of vitamins and minerals."
The supermodel said she eats meats like venison and turkey. (Getty Images for Christian Dior)
She said she drinks a 30-millimeter shot, and her youngest child has some as well, but she admitted her teenager is "not into it."
Kerr then has a marshmallow tea "because that’s good for the gut lining. S,o I get the marshmallow leaf, and then I put it and brew it in hot water."
That's followed by a few tablespoons of coconut yogurt with honey and a bite of a banana.
"I do all of this before I have my coffee. I get to my coffee, and my coffee is my moment where I’m in bliss," she admitted.
Her Fabula brand coffee, which she said is mold- and lead-free, includes coconut milk from high-end grocery store Erewhon and maple syrup.
She also doesn’t eat eggs.
"I do proteins, like meats like venison, bison, lamb, turkey. I eat all the meats that aren’t mass-produced for the reasons that we all know," she explained.
MIRANDA KERR'S HUSBAND, EVAN SPIEGEL, PRAISES HER 'VERY DIFFERENT' CO-PARENTING RELATIONSHIP WITH ORLANDO BLOOM
"I’m not much of a fruit girl, to be honest, but I will have a banana, and I also think a banana is a great snack to go," she said. "I do love mangoes."
She also stays away from dairy and wheat, "and I’m very specific about the oils, so only cooking with coconut oil or avocado oil. No seed oils."
Kerr said she does tallow sometimes, "mostly for the kids." She also tries to get them to eat sourdough because they refuse to eat gluten-free bread.
Miranda Kerr attends the Met Gala with husband Evan Spiegel. (FilmMagic)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Lots of squash, carrots and parsnips are also on the menu.
"And I do have a little bit of salmon but not too much because of the mercury that’s in salmon," she said.
The model said she used to "live on sushi" when she lived in New York, but she doesn't eat it anymore because of the possibility of parasites.
"I do love caviar," she admitted. "Caviar’s good. There’s no parasites there."

title: Rita Wilson ignored her mother's old-school marriage advice, and it led her to Tom Hanks
summary: Rita Wilson revealed on Michelle Obama's podcast the outdated marriage advice her mom gave before she found love with Tom Hanks on set in 1984.
story: Tom Hanks and wife Rita Wilson walked the pre-Grammy GALA red carpet discussing what they believe is the success to a great relationship after being married 34 years.
Rita Wilson is sharing the marriage advice her mom gave that didn't sit right with her.
During a recent appearance on Michelle Obama's podcast, "In My Opinion," the 69-year-old actress spoke about the outdated marriage advice her mom gave her before she met and married Tom Hanks.

"I was engaged before I got engaged to my husband. If I had married that person, I would have been divorced within a year," she said. "I thought that was what you were supposed to do at a certain age. I actually thought, because I had never really fallen in love with anyone, that I would be OK."

While engaged to that man, Wilson said she asked her mom for advice, telling her, "I don't know though. Should I marry him? I'm not really in love with him," and getting a surprising response in return.
Wilson shared she was engaged prior to meeting Tom Hanks and the marriage advice her mom gave her. (Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images)
'SHAMELESS' STAR EMMY ROSSUM REVEALS SECRET MARRIAGE AT 21 AFTER BOYFRIEND'S ALLEGED SHOCKING ULTIMATUM

"She said, 'Don't worry, you grow to love him.' I was like, 'Mom, that's not my generation,'" she said. "Her generation was like, 'Is he a good man? Will he provide?' There wasn't any of this, 'I have to be madly in love.' My parents were married for 59 years, so whatever they figured out, they figured out. But I still wanted to hold out for that falling in love thing."

Ultimately, Wilson did not go through with marrying the first man, knowing "marriage would not have sustained that relationship," and found love with Hanks after they reunited on set of "Volunteers" in 1984, tying the knot in 1988.

The "Now and Then" actress told Obama and her co-host and brother, Craig Robinson, when she "finally met Tom and fell in love with" Hanks, she had the feeling that "this is very, very different than what I had before."
When it comes to being a mom, Wilson said she wasn't sure she wanted to have children, but knew she "didn't wanna have children with the wrong people or person."

Hanks was already a father to Colin and Elizabeth, who he shares with his ex-wife, Samantha Lewes, and later welcomed sons Chet and Truman with Wilson.

Of his children, Colin and Chet have followed in Hanks and Wilson's footsteps, with Elizabeth pursuing a career as an author and journalist under the pen name E.A. Hanks and Truman focusing on other aspects of filmmaking.

title: Barry Manilow reschedules concert 45 minutes before start amid ongoing lung cancer recovery
summary: Barry Manilow reschedules his Lexington show just 45 minutes before showtime, citing unforeseen circumstances amid his ongoing lung cancer battle.
story: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel discusses iconic singer Barry Manilow’s cancer diagnosis on ‘America Reports.’
Barry Manilow rescheduled his Kentucky show on Tuesday just 45 minutes before it was set to start.

"Due to unforeseen circumstances tonight’s show in Lexington has been rescheduled," Manilow, who was diagnosed with lung cancer last year, wrote on X ahead of the concert. No other explanation was given.

Barry Manilow rescheduled his Kentucky show on Aug. 4 due to "unforeseen circumstances." (Scott Legato/Getty Images)

In December, Manilow revealed he had been diagnosed with early-stage lung cancer after doctors discovered a cancerous spot on his left lung following a bout of bronchitis.

"As many of you know I recently went through six weeks of bronchitis followed by a relapse of another five weeks," Manilow wrote on Instagram at the time. "Even though I was over the bronchitis and back on stage at the Westgate Las Vegas, my wonderful doctor ordered an MRI just to make sure that everything was OK. The MRI discovered a cancerous spot on my left lung that needs to be removed. It's pure luck (and a great doctor) that it was found so early. That's the good news."

"The doctors do not believe it has spread and I'm taking tests to confirm the diagnosis. So, that's it. No chemo. No radiation. Just chicken soup and I Love Lucy reruns."
In February, Manilow announced he was rescheduling additional February and March dates on the tour after a "very depressing visit" with his surgeon.

title: Perez Hilton under involuntary psych hold after apparent self-harm livestream: source
summary: Miami-Dade deputies responded to Perez Hilton's home after receiving multiple reports about an apparent self-harm incident during a TikTok livestream.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).Law enforcement was called to Perez Hilton's Miami residence after the celebrity blogger appeared to be harming himself during a TikTok livestream on Tuesday evening.

"The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office received multiple calls regarding an individual who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media," a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Deputies quickly located the individual’s residence, where they spoke with family members on scene, and confirmed he was alone inside.""In many incidents involving a person experiencing a mental health crisis or actively harming themselves, deputies prioritize de-escalation by creating time, distance, and opportunities for communication. Unless there is an immediate threat to others, slowing the situation and utilizing crisis intervention techniques can reduce the likelihood of a suicide-by-cop encounter and minimize the risk of injury to the individual, deputies, and the public."
CELEBRITY BLOGGER PEREZ HILTON SAYS HE FOUND GOD AMID MEDICAL SCARE IN EMOTIONAL CONFESSION
Law enforcement was called to Perez Hilton's Miami residence after the celebrity blogger appeared to be harming himself during a livestream. (Getty Images)
"At this time, deputies have tactically disengaged while continuing to monitor the situation and providing the needed support to his family," the statement concludes.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital that the individual had been "safely recovered and transported by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue to a local hospital, where he is receiving medical attention."
"The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office Crisis Response Unit and Licensed Mental Health Professionals are also on scene providing support and resources to the individual’s family."
A source close to the situation tells Fox News Digital that Hilton was placed under a psychiatric hold under the Baker Act and "had wounds and cuts all over the place."
"He’s alive," the source added. "He has superficial cuts all over the body."

The Florida Baker Act is a state law that gives law enforcement officers, judges and certain mental health professionals the authority to place an individual into an involuntary mental health evaluation when specific legal criteria are met.
Under the Baker Act, an individual can be transported to a designated receiving facility for an emergency psychiatric evaluation that generally lasts up to 72 hours.
On Wednesday, Hilton's family and team released a statement regarding his ongoing hospitalization.

"Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez, and we are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers," the statement read. "We can confirm that Perez is receiving medical care, and our family’s focus right now is on his well-being. We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time."
"If and when we are able to share any updates, we will do so with everyone as soon as we can," the statement concluded. "Thank you for your compassion, understanding, and continued support."
A representative for Hilton did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
The celebrity blogger was hospitalized earlier this year for severe sepsis and infections. (Ethan Miller/Getty Images)
The content creator recently moved to Miami with his mother, 73, and his three young children.

Hilton, born Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr., rose to fame in the mid-2000s after launching his celebrity gossip website in 2004. The Miami native quickly became one of the internet's most influential entertainment voices, known for breaking celebrity news and his unfiltered commentary.
The media personality has frequently shared how parenthood has reshaped his priorities, often offering followers a glimpse into family life on social media.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Earlier this year, Hilton revealed he had been hospitalized for 21 days after a severe case of sepsis stemming from complications related to the flu. The celebrity blogger said he developed an ulcer and stomach perforation after taking medication on an empty stomach, ultimately requiring emergency surgery and weeks of treatment.
In a candid video he shared at the time, he said God had "presented himself to me" during the ordeal and changed him through the experience.
"God presented himself to me and then did something. Something I can only call miraculous... it was real, and this has been life-changing," he said.
In a follow-up video, the entertainment columnist tearfully apologized for past mistakes and said he had begun reading the Bible again.

"I’ve been crying, but happy tears. Happy tears. Because this is just, this is just so crazy. I’ve been reading the Bible, and so much of what is said here I had already been thinking of. It’s just overwhelming in the best, most beautiful way," he said while holding up a Bible to the camera.

"I made a lot of mistakes in my past. We all have. Nobody's perfect," he said. "But my mistakes are very public. The internet is forever. Receipts are forever. I carry with me deep shame and regret. I'm sorry. I will continue to apologize. I have also reached out to make amends. I've apologized publicly and privately to dozens of people."
Hilton recently said he found God amid a medical scare in an emotional confession. (Gabe Ginsberg/Getty Images)

"Because I was so selfish, because I didn't care who I hurt. I just cared about the views, the attention, the money — people hated me," he continued. "Some people enjoyed it, but it felt like most people hated me. And last week, since I've been home, I haven't been getting as much hate, and I've been getting love and prayers."

Hilton added, "And I know that some people are fed up with me talking about God. You don’t have to watch these videos. You don’t have to watch. I love God. My experience was real. My testimony is important."

"What matters is today. How I behave today, how I behave tomorrow," he continued. "And not only did God save me in so many ways, but God gave me a new lease on life and a new opportunity to truly be better and do better."

title: Ariana Grande sets record straight after announcing break from spotlight
summary: PR expert says Ariana Grande's strategic absence after her "Eternal Sunshine Tour" could build anticipation and make her return an event.
story: A ‘Fox News @ Night’ panel analyzes celebrity support for anti-I.C.E. protests and reactions to Don Lemon’s arrest.
Ariana Grande is taking control of her own narrative.

While performing in Chicago on Monday, the Grammy Award winner addressed concertgoers directly after news broke that she plans to take a break from all public appearances and performances once her "Eternal Sunshine Tour" wraps up next month.

"Sometimes when a story comes out that's not directly from me, things can get a little blown out of proportion, so I just wanted to speak to my fans directly tonight because I love you so much," Grande told the crowd, according to multiple videos shared on social media.

"The announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing. It was something that I had decided, it's a plan that I had quietly made a long time ago. It was a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place. And I want you to know that many things can be true at the same time."
ARIANA GRANDE FIGHTS BACK AGAINST BODY-SHAMERS AS CRITICS COMMENT ON HER WEIGHT DURING 'WICKED' PRESS TOUR
Ariana Grande plans on "taking a step back from visibility" amid "ongoing public scrutiny." (WWD via Getty Images)
Grande's comments came one day after her representative confirmed to People magazine that the singer will step away from the public eye for a while.

"Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the ‘Eternal Sunshine Tour’," Grande's representative told the outlet. "She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER
"This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much," the representative added.

The planned hiatus is already affecting Grande's schedule. According to People, the singer will no longer appear in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim's "Sunday in the Park with George" next summer.
The pop star's "Eternal Sunshine Tour" is expected to wrap next month. (Getty Images)
Addressing fans in Chicago, Grande acknowledged that many had worried the decision was fueled by negativity.
"I just have to say that could not be more the f--- opposite," she said. "This is not what that is."

She continued, "Multiple things can be true at the same time: boundaries need to be set, human beings can need a break sometimes… and also, this can be and will continue to be the greatest experience of my professional and creative life."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Sometimes when a story comes out that's not directly from me, things can get a little blown out of proportion, so I just wanted to speak to my fans directly tonight because I love you so much," Grande told the audience at her show. (Presley Ann/Getty Images for DAOU Vineyards)
Grande ended the emotional moment by calling the tour "the most healing, beautiful, corrective, magnificent, special experience of my life."
While the singer insisted the break had been planned long before it became public, PR expert Steve Honig believes the timing could ultimately strengthen her career.

"Stepping back from the spotlight can strengthen Ariana Grande's brand because she has reached a level of stardom where she can take a break without hurting her career," Honig, founder of The Honig Company, told Fox News Digital. "In today's nonstop media environment, Grande's scarcity will build anticipation and give audiences a chance to miss her. From a public relations standpoint, a strategic absence can create more value than constant visibility, making her eventual return feel like an event."
Grande hopes to wrap her tour on "a high note," despite the growing speculation surrounding her health. (WireImage)
According to Honig, only a select group of entertainers can successfully disappear from public view without losing momentum.

"Whether stepping away from the spotlight helps a celebrity's career depends largely on how established they are and the strength of their personal brand," he explained. "Celebrities who have reached high levels of fame can afford to take a break because they have built loyal audiences and lasting relevance. In many cases, absence really does make the heart grow fonder."
Grande's announcement follows months of online discussion surrounding her appearance, something the "Wicked: For Good" star has addressed publicly on multiple occasions.
Last year, Grande reshared a previous message on her Instagram Story urging people to stop commenting on others' bodies.
SUPERMODEL SLAMS GLP-1 TREND, SAYS WEIGHT LOSS SHOTS ARE A 'SMACK IN THE FACE' TO BODY POSITIVITY MOVEMENT
Grande addressed the announcement during her show in Chicago on Monday. (Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic)
"Resharing this from last year as a loving reminder to all," she wrote alongside a clip of a December 2024 interview with Cynthia Erivo.
In the video, Grande reflected on growing up in the spotlight.

"I've been doing this in front of the public and been a specimen in a Petri dish really since I was 16 or 17, so I have heard it all," she said. "I've heard every version of it, of what's wrong with me, and then you fix it, and then it's wrong for different reasons."
She added that criticism about a person's appearance can be damaging regardless of their level of fame.
"It's hard to protect yourself from that noise," Grande said. "It's something that is uncomfortable no matter what scale you're experiencing it on."
Grande has been open about the struggles of living in the public eye. (Suhaimi Abdullah/Getty Images)
Honig said Grande's previous comments underscore one of the biggest branding challenges celebrities face when public attention shifts away from their work.

"When the conversation shifts from a celebrity's work to their appearance, regaining control of the narrative becomes much more difficult because appearance becomes the basis for discussion," he said. "The best way to change the conversation is not by responding to every criticism, but by addressing the issue with facts and giving people something else to focus on."
He added that prolonged speculation can ultimately reshape how audiences perceive a celebrity if left unanswered.

"The biggest branding challenge is maintaining a clear and consistent brand identity when public attention is focused on the wrong thing," Honig said. "Instead of being known for their talent, the celebrity risks becoming associated with superficial distractions that dilute their brand."
PR expert Steve Honig says Grande's break could be a positive step in the pop star's career. (Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for The Met Museum/Vogue)
Still, Honig believes Grande's decision to address the speculation directly during Monday's concert was the right move.

"In the majority of cases, it is better for a celebrity to directly address any sort of negative speculation," he said. "By doing this, the celebrity will pretty much shut down the speculation, replacing it with facts. Left unanswered, speculation often takes on a life of its own and can become accepted as truth simply through repetition."

For Grande, however, Honig believes the planned hiatus won't diminish her career in any way.
"Stepping back only works when a celebrity has reached the point where they have earned the luxury of being missed," he said. "Ariana Grande is one of those celebrities."

title: Zoe Saldaña says Taylor Sheridan gives stars two choices: 'Make sure that you don't f--k up... or you quit'
summary: Zoe Saldaña says Taylor Sheridan gives actors two choices on his sets: accept the challenge or quit. The "Lioness" star reveals his approach.
story: Zoe Saldana admitted to Fox News Digital that she "wished" she knew how to balance raising her three sons while maintaining a career in Hollywood.
Taylor Sheridan gives actors what Zoe Saldaña says are one of two choices on set.
The "Lioness" star offered a rare glimpse into what it's like working with the prolific writer, director and producer, saying his standards challenge every actor who steps onto one of his sets.

"So working with him is a challenge in the sense that he does raise the bar," Saldaña told People magazine. "And you have one of two choices. You either accept the challenge and make sure that you don't f--- up... or you quit."
"And I like being challenged," she added. "I really do."
ZOE SALDAÑA SAYS TAYLOR SHERIDAN 'REALLY SEES WOMEN' AS LIONESS SEASON THREE HITS PARAMOUNT+
Zoe Saldaña as Joe in Lioness season 3, streaming on Paramount+, 2026. (Lauren Smith/Paramount+)

Saldaña's comments come as Sheridan continues to build one of television's biggest entertainment empires with hit series including "Yellowstone," "Lioness," "Landman," "Tulsa King," "Mayor of Kingstown" and the "Yellowstone" prequels. His challenging scripts and hands-on approach have earned him a reputation for pushing actors to elevate their performances.
For Saldaña, who stars as CIA operative Joe McNamara in Paramount+'s "Lioness," those expectations begin long before cameras start rolling.
TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S 'LIONESS' SEASON 3 IS AN ACTION-PACKED SAGA LOADED WITH VIOLENCE AND CARNAGE
Speaking recently with USA TODAY, the Oscar-winning actress recalled Sheridan personally calling her ahead of season three to prepare her for the physically demanding role.
"He said, 'I definitely want you to build more muscle. I want Joe to be just a machine,'" Saldaña told the outlet.
The actress said she immediately hired a private trainer to help transform into the battle-hardened CIA operative before filming began.
Sheridan's presence on set can also be intimidating.

Zoe Saldaña opened up about working with Taylor Sheridan, saying the "Lioness" creator challenges actors while remaining collaborative on set. (Dia Dipasupil/WireImage/Getty Images; Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for Viacom/Getty Images)
"Sheridan is an intimidating cat," Saldaña told USA TODAY. "I'm not going to lie. And he comes in so serious. It raises the bar for the rest of us."
Despite his demanding reputation, Saldaña told People magazine the "Yellowstone" creator is equally committed to collaborating with actors who come prepared.

"It's actually great," she said of working directly with Sheridan. "When you work with him is when you realize how passionate he is about actors and about acting. I think it is his first love when it comes to the arts."

"He's an incredibly smart person. He's very curious about government affairs, and he seeks out information and education based on that curiosity," Saldaña continued. "And then he writes these incredibly elaborate shows that end up really educating us as well."
According to Saldaña, Kidman has become one of her closest collaborators on the series.
Nicole Kidman and Zoe Saldaña attend Paramount+'s "Lioness" Season 3 New York premiere at SVA Theater on July 29, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)
The actresses told People they have developed a routine whenever Sheridan's complex scripts leave them searching for answers.
"We tag team finding out where Taylor is and seeing if he's going to call us back because, when we need him, it's always having to do with the work," Saldaña said.

After spending "five or ten minutes" catching up every morning, the pair head to hair and makeup before turning their attention to the day's scenes, often tracking Sheridan down between takes to discuss dialogue that "don't feel like they're making any sense."
WATCH NOW: LAYSLA DE OLIVEIRA AND JILL WAGNER TALK 'LIONESS' SEASON THREE
For Saldaña, that teamwork has become one of the highlights of making the series.

"And she plays all of those roles beautifully," Saldaña continued. "And she does it with so much love and unconditional support. That's admirable. So everything about working with Nicole has been true joy."
Kidman returned the compliment.
'LIONESS' STAR JILL WAGNER CHOSE TENNESSEE FARM LIFE TO RAISE HER FAMILY

title: Eating too much protein could backfire, experts warn after longevity review
summary: Excess protein may strain the body in sedentary people, but adding exercise and plant-based protein sources could unlock compounding longevity benefits.
story: Instead of restricting foods, dietitian Tanya Freirich recommends building a balanced plate with vegetables, protein and starch, and swapping some animal protein for beans, lentils, nuts or seeds to support better health.

A recent scientific review challenged the idea that consuming more protein necessarily leads to better health, suggesting that the optimal amount depends on factors such as age, activity level and overall health.

After reviewing more than 350 studies, researchers at the University of Wisconsin-Madison concluded that while higher protein intake can support muscle growth and other health benefits, consuming more than the body needs may offer little advantage.
In fact, it could even reduce longevity in some sedentary adults, particularly when protein comes from certain sources or amino acid profiles, they concluded.
LIVING LONGER COULD HINGE ON ONE SURPRISING DIETARY CHANGE, STUDY REVIEW SUGGESTS
For those wondering how to adjust their own diets in light of these findings, the answer lies in personalization, activity level and food sources, according to experts.
"We are hearing conflicting things from doctors ... and influencers," Tanya Freirich, a registered dietitian nutritionist in Charlotte, North Carolina, told Fox News Digital.
People who are active can still benefit from higher protein intake, the expert said. (iStock)
"The message lately has been to increase your protein," said the expert, who was not involved in the research.
"However, we do know that excess protein is associated with negative effects. It can put a strain on your kidney health, and it can interfere with bone and calcium homeostasis."
POPULAR SMOOTHIE INGREDIENT MAY REDUCE ONE KEY HEALTH BENEFIT, STUDY SUGGESTS
For sedentary individuals, cutting back on excess protein isn’t the only option, according to Freirich. Increasing physical activity can also help the body use nutrients more effectively.
"If you are moving your body — strength training, building muscle or doing sports — you probably do need a little bit more protein," she noted.
"Everyone should think about their personal situation and discuss it with healthcare providers to figure out the best route for them."

"Now, let's say you were a super active person and unfortunately had an injury and have gone down to a very sedentary level — you should modify your protein because your body is not utilizing it in the same way."
Exercise may also support longevity in ways that go beyond nutrition, Freirich noted, by helping people stay active and independent.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Adding exercise is always a good idea because it is associated with having fewer falls, having more joy in life and protecting you from injury," she said.

The recent analysis suggests that high-protein diets could have negative effects on longevity in sedentary individuals whose bodies are not actively using the extra nutrients to build or repair muscle. (iStock)
For those looking to rebalance their nutrition without doing a total overhaul, Freirich offered the following five tips.
No. 1: Focus on plate proportions: Aim for 50% of your plate to consist of vegetables, 25% protein and 25% starches or whole grains.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

No. 2: Do the quick math: A general guideline is to consume 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day for adults with lower activity levels, while those who are more physically active may benefit from about 1.0 gram per kilogram per day.
No. 3: Eat the rainbow: Incorporate fruits and vegetables across various colors to ensure a diverse intake of vitamins and micro-nutrients.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

No. 4: Switch to plant proteins: Shift a portion of animal protein toward plant-based alternatives like lentils, beans, chickpeas and seeds. "A lot of people who were on protein-restricted diets and saw better health outcomes were eating a lot of their proteins from plants," Freirich noted.

No. 5: Stick to whole foods: Unprocessed foods support natural satiety signals. "Moving away from really processed foods to more unprocessed foods actually helps your body regulate a lot better," Freirich advised.
Swapping animal proteins for plant-based sources like beans, lentils and seeds provides alternative amino acid profiles alongside fiber, the nutritionist said. (iStock)
Ultimately, dietary choices shouldn't be governed by a single headline or study, according to the expert.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Research is ever-evolving," Freirich said. "Everyone should think about their personal situation and discuss it with healthcare providers to figure out the best route for them."

title: FDA approves first-ever mRNA flu vaccine for millions of older Americans
summary: A new mRNA flu vaccine showed a 27% reduction in flu cases in a clinical trial, but its path to FDA approval faced an early regulatory setback.
story: An experimental pancreatic cancer vaccine shows promise in its first human trial, generating an immune response in 90% of high-risk patients.
The FDA has approved the nation's first flu vaccine made with mRNA technology, the manufacturer, Moderna, announced on Thursday.
The vaccine, which is based on the same messenger RNA platform used in COVID-19 shots, has been fully approved for adults ages 50-64 ahead of the 2026-2027 flu season.
For adults 65 and older, the vaccine received accelerated approval, which allows the vaccine to be used while Moderna completes an additional study to confirm its effectiveness in seniors.
PANCREATIC CANCER VACCINE SHOWS PROMISE IN FIRST HUMAN TRIAL, PREVENTING DISEASE IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS
Experts say mRNA vaccines can be updated more quickly to protect against changes in circulating flu strains.
The approval was based on a phase 3 clinical trial including around 40,000 participants, in which the new vaccine was found to effect a 27% reduction in flu cases compared to a standard flu vaccine.
The FDA has approved the nation's first flu vaccine made with mRNA technology, the manufacturer, Moderna, announced on Thursday. (iStock)
No major safety concerns were identified in the trial, according to the announcement.
It was found to have more short-term side effects than conventional flu shots – including arm pain, fatigue, headache and fever – although these were noted to be generally mild and temporary.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
"This is not a universal vaccine, but is geared for rapid turnaround once the yearly strains have been identified," said Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst.
"It’s similar to the COVID vaccine and was found to be 25% to 30% more effective than the current flu vaccine," he added. "It’s geared to protect the elderly."
Experts say mRNA vaccines can be updated more quickly to protect against changes in circulating flu strains. (iStock)

Older adults face the biggest risk of severe influenza. During the 2024-2025 season, people 65 and older accounted for 57% of flu-related hospitalizations and 71% of deaths, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
An estimated 51 million Americans contracted the flu during the 2024-2025 season, with the virus linked to around 710,000 hospitalizations and 45,000 deaths, per the above source.
Looking ahead, the approval could pave the way for combination vaccines that protect against multiple respiratory viruses at once, according to Moderna. (Reuters/Brian Snyder)

Earlier this year, the new mRNA vaccine faced a regulatory setback when the FDA initially refused to review Moderna's application, citing concerns about the design of its clinical trial, the Associated Press reported.
Moderna disputed the decision, and the FDA later agreed to move forward with the review.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
In June, an independent FDA advisory committee agreed that the vaccine's benefits outweighed its risks, paving the way for its approval.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Looking ahead, the approval could pave the way for combination vaccines that protect against multiple respiratory viruses at once, according to Moderna.
The company said it is pursuing a combined flu/COVID vaccine, with the goal of giving people one seasonal shot.

title: FDA widens cyclospora outbreak investigation to six more states as confirmed cases top 6,000
summary: The FDA says 6,358 cyclospora cases are now linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico, with 278 hospitalizations and two deaths.
story: Panelists debate whether more government is really the answer to controlling the outbreak.
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) expanded its investigation of the cyclospora outbreak on Wednesday, announcing that there are thousands of confirmed cases across more than a dozen states.

The intestinal illness was first reported in July among people who developed severe diarrhea after eating shredded lettuce at Taco Bell. Health authorities later traced the outbreak to contaminated lettuce supplied to the fast-food restaurant by Taylor Farms de Mexico.
"Due to the additional interview data, the outbreak now includes people who reported exposure to Taco Bell or recalled Taylor Farms de Mexico iceberg lettuce," the FDA said in a news release.

According to the FDA, 6,358 cases have now been reported across 15 states. Six states — Arkansas, Iowa, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire and North Carolina — were added since the administration’s previous update on July 24.
CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK: IS IT STILL SAFE TO EAT AT RESTAURANTS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW
A crop of lettuce is watered in Bakersfield, California, in 2021. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The FDA said the outbreak began on June 22, nearly a month before Taylor Farms de Mexico voluntarily recalled all lettuce sourced from central Mexico on July 17.
Since then, cyclosporiasis has been linked to 278 hospitalizations and two deaths in Michigan, according to the FDA.

"We also expect to continue to see the number of confirmed cases rise, despite the recall, due to the fact that it can take as long as six weeks for CDC and state officials to determine if a sick person is part of this outbreak," the FDA said.
A massive surge in cyclospora cases means people may be mistaking this parasitic foodborne infection for a standard summer stomach bug. (iStock)
SENATE CONFIRMS NEW CDC DIRECTOR AS DIARRHEA-CAUSING PARASITE OUTBREAK SWEEPS US

Cyclospora is a single-celled parasite that can cause stomach cramps, nausea, fatigue, weight loss and other health problems, though some infected people remain asymptomatic, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
Symptoms usually begin about one week after being infected and can last for a few days to a month, according to the CDC. Symptoms can also appear to go away before returning one or more times.
Man sits on a bed and holds his stomach while home alone. Cyclospora can cause stomach cramps, as well as a number of other symptoms. (iStock)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The FDA again urged consumers and retailers to throw away contaminated lettuce, including Marketside-branded products sold in grocery stores across 27 states in early July.
Health officials also recommend sanitizing any surfaces that came into contact with the lettuce and contacting a doctor if symptoms develop after eating it.

title: Popular smoothie ingredient may reduce one key health benefit, study suggests
summary: A viral video claims bananas degrade blueberry benefits in smoothies, based on recent research, but dietitians argue that fruit shouldn't be villainized.
story: Registered dietitian nutritionist Ilana Muhlstein weighs in on claims that bananas reduce the health benefits of berries in smoothies, noting that the current research shouldn't be overstated.
Bananas are a smoothie staple, but a viral social media video has raised questions about whether they could reduce the nutritional benefits of other ingredients, such as blueberries.

In a July appearance on the "Mel Robbins Podcast," Dr. Rhonda Patrick, a biomedical scientist and founder of FoundMyFitness, demonstrated how she likes to make her smoothies, which do not include bananas.

Bananas contain polyphenol oxidase (PPO), an enzyme that can break down polyphenols, which are beneficial for gut, heart and brain health, according to Patrick, who is based in San Diego. PPO is also responsible for turning cut fruit brown.
DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE
Recent studies suggest that when a banana is added to a blueberry smoothie, fewer beneficial polyphenols are absorbed from the berries.
Bananas contain polyphenol oxidase (PPO), an enzyme that can break down polyphenols in fruits like blueberries, which are beneficial for gut, heart and brain health. (iStock)

Instead, Patrick uses avocado to give the smoothie the same creamy texture with 95% less sugar, she said. Avocado also adds more vitamins and monounsaturated fat, which can increase absorption of carotenoids, like lutein and zeaxanthin, from kale in the smoothie.
This opinion sparked debate in the online nutrition community, with some dietitians and nutritionists arguing that bananas should not be villainized based on a small body of research.
STUDY FINDS SPECIAL TOMATO DRINK MAY REDUCE INFLAMMATION IN ADULTS WITH OBESITY
The study Patrick referenced, which was published in the journal Food & Function in 2023, analyzed food absorption in eight healthy men.

On separate days, participants drank either a banana smoothie (high in an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase), drank a mixed berry smoothie (low in the enzyme) or took flavan-3-ol capsules (dietary supplements that contain concentrated plant compounds) with milk.
Study results revealed that the banana smoothie produced a peak concentration of polyphenols that were about 84% lower than the flavan-3-ol capsules. (iStock)
Blood tests showed that people absorbed about 84% fewer beneficial plant compounds after drinking the banana smoothie than after taking the flavan-3-ol capsules.
While researchers didn't test a banana-blueberry smoothie, the results suggest that bananas could reduce the benefits of foods high in flavan-3-ols.
LIVING LONGER COULD HINGE ON SURPRISING DIETARY CHANGE, STUDY REVIEW SUGGESTS
Los Angeles-based registered dietitian nutritionist Ilana Muhlstein, author of the upcoming book "Beyond the Shot," said the findings are "interesting," but don't tell the whole story.
"It doesn't mean the smoothie loses all of its health benefits," she said. "You're still getting fiber from the banana, and many other beneficial nutrients from polyphenol-rich fruits."

Muhlstein pointed out that the study included only eight participants and has not yet been replicated. She also noted that researchers used a standardized cocoa-derived flavanol supplement instead of whole fruits, such as berries, which may be absorbed differently by the body.
While researchers didn't test a banana-blueberry smoothie, the results suggest that bananas could reduce the benefits of foods high in flavan-3-ols. (iStock)

In a follow-up post on Instagram, responding to the backlash from the original post, Patrick said, "You can add bananas to your blueberry smoothies. However, you should know that you are going to degrade some of the polyphenols in those blueberries."

"Bananas are nutritious, I eat them, and this is not a reason to stop," she added in the caption. "But if your goal is to preserve as many of the berry polyphenols as possible, the chemistry matters."
POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY HELP PROTECT AGAINST A DEADLY DISEASE, DOCTOR SAYS
Not every beneficial compound in blueberries will be eliminated by bananas, Patrick wrote, as the fruit contains many other polyphenols, including anthocyanins.
"This was a small study that should be replicated," she said. "But the magnitude of the effect was meaningful enough for me to consider when optimizing my smoothie."
New York-based certified holistic nutritionist Robin DeCicco agreed that the findings don't mean everyone should avoid bananas.
Unlike well-established advice to limit processed meats and added sugar, the guidance on bananas is more nuanced and doesn't apply to everyone, she told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
As nutrition advice spreads on social media, DeCicco said it's important to remember that everyone's health needs are different and to consult a doctor before following online recommendations.

The broader issue, she noted, is that Americans aren’t eating enough nutrient-rich foods, like bananas and berries, and are instead consuming more processed foods that have been linked to chronic disease.
"It doesn't need to be so complicated all the time," a nutritionist said. "If you're eating a banana instead of french fries, that's good." (iStock)

"That’s why Americans are fatter and sicker than they've ever been, so I think focus on that more," DeCicco advised. "It doesn't need to be so complicated all the time … If you're eating a banana instead of french fries, that's good."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Nutrition should be individualized, DeCicco said. Someone who eats mostly fast-food should focus on replacing processed foods with fruits and vegetables, while someone with a more advanced nutrition plan may benefit from limiting high-carb, high-sugar fruits like bananas.

For those trying to lose weight and balance blood sugar, choosing fruits that are lower in sugar and higher in fiber may help with these outcomes.
"It really [depends] on where you're coming from and what your health journey is," DeCicco said.
Those who are looking to maximize their polyphenol intake can use frozen zucchini, avocado or Greek yogurt in place of banana in a smoothie, nutritionists say. (iStock)
