A Justice Department spokesperson later said that they received the referral “and will work with the Senate accordingly.”

If Paul did ask the full Senate to vote on the resolution, it probably would not have enough support to clear the 60-vote threshold that would be needed for the measure to pass in the narrowly divided chamber.

If Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, chooses to try to prosecute the case, her office would need to secure an indictment from a grand jury in the district, where she has a mixed track record.
In a statement, Fauci’s lawyer called the vote “a crude political stunt intended to punish Dr. Fauci for exercising his constitutional rights.”

“Today’s resolution is a continuation of Senator Paul’s personal vendetta against Dr. Fauci, who spent 50 years in public health and has saved countless lives,” the lawyer, David Schertler, said. “It is shameful and wrong that Senator Paul is abusing his power by trying to weaponize the Justice Department against an honorable public servant.”

Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich., said in his opening remarks at the meeting that the committee vote would create a “damaging precedent” that would cause future congressional witnesses to resist providing testimony.

“If this committee now seeks to punish a witness for asserting their constitutional protected Fifth Amendment rights, future witnesses will argue that appearing before Congress exposes them to punishment, regardless of whether they comply with the subpoena and invoke a constitutional protection,” said Peters, the top Democrat on the committee.
“They will point directly to this vote, this vote, as a justification for refusing to appear at all,” Peters said.
As the meeting progressed, Democrats called for votes to table the contempt resolution five times — a push that was rejected along party lines.
Paul has argued that Fauci, the former head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, could not invoke the Fifth Amendment right because of his pre-emptive pardon from Biden.

“I ordered him to answer and warned him about contempt, yet he still refused,” Paul said in a statement Tuesday. “That is obstruction of a congressional investigation. The Committee will act accordingly.”

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said in remarks before the committee vote that his investigation of Fauci has “just begun.” Johnson’s office announced Wednesday that the subcommittee he leads has obtained a copy of Fauci’s iPhone. Fauci used the phone when serving in the Department of Health and Human Services during the pandemic.

“We’ve invited Dr. Fauci for a transcribed interview,” Johnson said. “OK, he doesn’t want to do it in front of the American public. Come in front of our committee. You say you have nothing to hide. Good. We’ll do it behind closed doors. We’ll transcribe it. That’s only one of the interviews we’ll be conducting.”

Republicans also argued in pressing for the contempt resolution that Fauci effectively “waived” his Fifth Amendment right by delivering “his opening testimony on subject matter pertinent to the questions under inquiry.”
Abbe Smith, a Georgetown Law professor, said Republicans’ claims about Fauci’s inability to invoke the Fifth did not seem correct.

“There would have to be some sort of legal understanding about the nature of the pardon and whether it is limitless, and those pre-emptive pardons, those are unique,” she said. “I’m not sure anybody knows how much protection they provide.”
Smith said she, too, would have advised Fauci to assert the Fifth had she been his defense counsel.

Smith said Republicans’ argument that Fauci’s opening statement meant he waived his Fifth Amendment right was “a little more interesting, but ultimately specious in my view,” because Fauci used his opening statement to point to his public service, belief in accountability and previous congressional testimony while explaining that “this is a bridge too far.”
“I don’t think that sort of an opening statement is a waiver,” she said. “It’s not like he was answering specific allegations and then shutting down questioning.”

Thursday’s vote is the latest salvo in Republicans’ campaign against Fauci, which has been building for years in the wake of anti-lockdown sentiment and fierce debate over the origins of the virus. Paul has targeted Fauci for years, clashing with the doctor in previous congressional hearings and repeatedly accusing him of lying, which Fauci has denied.

On Tuesday, Paul accused Fauci of committing felonies, alleging again that the doctor lied to Congress and destroyed records. Asked in an interview on MS NOW whether he believes Fauci should go to prison, Paul said it was “a good question.”

“Did he lie to Congress?” Paul asked. “I think he did lie to Congress, and I think to be fair, that people who lie to Congress should be charged with a felony, and if convicted, go to jail. There’s also the question of destroying records. That’s also a felony crime. So I think both destroying records and lying to Congress are serious crimes.”

Fauci and his lawyers have rejected Paul’s repeated claims. In a statement last week, Schertler, Fauci’s lawyer, said that Paul’s “public crusade against Dr. Fauci can only be described as an obsessive vendetta.”
During last week’s hearing, Republicans repeatedly attacked Fauci over his leadership during the pandemic. Democrats defended Fauci and criticized the premise of the hearing as a fishing expedition.

“Given Sen. Paul’s obvious obsession with calling for my prosecution, his repeated slanderous comments about me, and recently his publicly releasing my unredacted personal diary aimed at embarrassing and intimidating me, the only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, ‘behind bars,’ unquote,” Fauci said.

title: Appeals court blocks Trump’s White House ballroom construction
summary: A federal appeals court affirmed a federal judge’s ruling to block construction of the White House ballroom while allowing below-ground construction to move forward.
story: A federal appeals court on Friday affirmed a U.S. judge’s ruling to block construction of the White House ballroom while allowing below-ground work to move forward.

In a 2-1 decision, the court affirmed the modified preliminary injunction issued by U.S. District Judge Richard Leon. But they stayed their own ruling for 14 days to allow the Trump administration to appeal the case to the Supreme Court.
The White House did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment.
“Whether or not a massive ballroom should be constructed is for Congress to decide and is not a matter for Executive self-help,” the appeals court’s ruling said.

That’s because the “Constitution assigns Congress — not the Executive — the responsibility to decide whether proposed changes to the physical design of the White House may proceed, even where those changes are said to serve security interests.”

“Each President is a temporary tenant, not the owner, of the White House and its Executive Residence,” the Ruling said. “The President has no — and claims no — constitutionally assigned authority over that property.”
The ruling paints the current administration as completely ignoring those restrictions.

“Over just three days in October 2025, without undertaking promised consultations or obtaining Congress’s permission, President Trump bulldozed the entire East Wing in order to construct a massive, 90,000 square-foot ballroom paid for by private funds with no congressional oversight,” it said.

“We are aware of no instance in American history in which a President unilaterally and using privately collected funds demolished substantial portions of the White House that Congress authorized to be built and American taxpayers paid for. Until now.”

The ruling by U.S. Circuit Judges Patricia Millett, an Obama appointee, and Brad Garcia, a Biden appointee, says it “has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the Defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom.

“What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court’s expeditious litigation without securing Congress’s authorization, as the Constitution and laws require,” they wrote.

The dissenting judge was Trump appointee Neomi Rao, who said the lower court had “abused its discretion in seizing control of construction at the President’s home and office” through the underlying order that her colleagues were upholding.

That judge had previously let some aspects of the construction to move forward, but then said the Trump administration was taking advantage of a safety and security exception to encompass the entire ballroom construction effort.

“Defendants argue that the entire ballroom construction project, from tip to tail, falls within the safety-and-security exception and therefore may proceed unabated. That is neither a reasonable nor a correct reading of my Order!”Leon, a noted fan of exclamation marks, wrote in his prior April order.
“It is, to say the least, incredible, if not disingenuous, that Defendants now argue that my Order does not stop ballroom construction because of the safety-and-security exception!” he added.

title: Perez Hilton’s family says his children ‘fled’ their home before his reported self-harm livestream
summary: The family said they “fled to protect from witnessing any further trauma” after “it became clear” that Hilton was “harming himself.”
story: Perez Hilton’s family said his three children, niece and sister were inside the home “minutes before” he publicly livestreamed what appeared to be self-harm amid “a severe mental health crisis.”
In a statement issued Thursday on Hilton’s blog, his family said they “fled to protect from witnessing any further trauma” after “it became clear” that Hilton was “harming himself.”

Hilton, 48, whose real name is Mario Lavandeira, started a livestream on his TikTok account Tuesday before the platform pulled it and his account down. In the video, he appeared to be covered in blood, with visible cuts and holding what appeared to be a knife.

The celebrity blogger is a single parent to his children, who are all under the age of 14 and born via surrogacy. Hilton’s family implored the public “to leave the area surrounding the family’s home and not return.”

“Our highest priority right now is helping the children begin to heal from what they experienced,” the statement reads. “An important part of that process is allowing them to safely return home and begin rebuilding a sense of security and normalcy.”

A spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office told NBC News that deputies responded to reports Tuesday night of someone “who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media.” The office did not name Hilton, but it said the person was “safely recovered” and taken by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue to a hospital, where he was receiving medical attention.
Hilton’s family confirmed he was receiving medical care Wednesday, saying he “is able to communicate, which has given our family hope.”

The 48-year-old was hospitalized at least two times in the months preceding this week’s incident for an ulcer, sepsis and deep vein thrombosis. In recent months, he has also told his followers that he’s found God.

Hilton rose to fame in the early 2000s blogging about celebrities’ personal lives and other entertainment news. His work has often been criticized for belittling women and invading the privacy of others.
On Thursday, his family expressed gratitude “for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers we have received during this incredibly difficult time.”
“The events of the past several days have been nearly unbearable for our family,” the statement reads.
If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 or go to 988lifeline.org to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Woman who killed husband over two decades ago admits to fatally stabbing firefighter wife
summary: A woman in California admitted on Tuesday that she stabbed her wife to death last year, more than two decades after facing prison time for killing her ex-husband in a similar manner.
story: A woman in California admitted on Tuesday that she stabbed her wife to death last year, more than two decades after facing prison time for killing her ex-husband in a similar manner.

Yolanda Olejniczak Marodi, 54, pleaded guilty to second-degree murder in connection with the the death of her wife, Rebecca “Becky” Marodi, 49, a respected California firefighter. She was arrested in connection with the crime last year after fleeing to Mexico.

Rebecca Marodi was found dead in her San Diego County home on Feb. 17, 2025, with several injuries to her neck, chest and back “consistent with a stabbing,” the San Diego County Sheriff’s Office said at the time.
Her wife “was seen on surveillance video earlier in the evening arguing with Rebecca and physically assaulting her,” according to the sheriff’s office.

Rebecca Marodi’s mother, Lorena Marodi, found her daughter with multiple stab wounds and called for help, according to the sheriff’s office. Life saving measures were performed on site, but Rebecca Marodi succumbed to her injuries.

Yolanda Marodi was captured by Mexican officials in the country more than a month later before being brought back the United States. She was found at a hotel roughly 2.3 miles south of the U.S. border in the city of Mexicali, the Baja California Citizen Security Secretariat (SSCBC) said at the time.

An affidavit for Yolanda Marodi’s arrest describes Ring security video captured outside the couple’s home in Ramona, California — about 45 miles northeast of San Diego — on the day that the firefighter was slain.

The document said Rebecca Marodi could be seen with blood on her back and was heard on the video saying, “Yolanda! Please … (I) don’t want to die.” Yolanda Marodi, seen in the video holding a knife, responded, “You should have thought about that before.”
Later, she can be seen wearing different clothes and packing  her silver Chevrolet Equinox SUV before driving away, according to the document.

In 2003, Yolanda Marodi pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter in the stabbing death of husband Jim Olejniczak in 2000, according to NBC San Diego. She was released from custody a decade later, according to the station.
Lorena Marodi told authorities that her daughter informed Yolanda Marodi about a week before the killing that she was ending the marriage, according to the affidavit.

“Becky came home and told me she was leaving, she met someone else, all the messages were lies,” Yolanda Marodi wrote to an unnamed associate the day after the killing, according to the affidavit. “We had a big fight and I hurt her…I’m sorry.”

Rebecca Marodi worked in firefighting for more than 30 years, starting as a volunteer in Moreno Valley, according to a joint statement from the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, known as Cal Fire, and the Riverside County Fire Department.

The 49-year-old was on the frontlines of the Eaton Fire — one of the state’s deadliest blazes in recent years — last year, according to an Instagram post from Cal Fire’s battalion in Temecula, California, a community about 65 miles north of San Diego.
“Becky was a beloved member of our community and Department, and we miss her greatly,” Cal Fire/Riverside County Fire Department said in a statement after Rebecca Marodi’s killing last year.

title: Do Owen and Allie End Up Together in ‘One Night Only’? Director Breaks Down the Unexpected Ending
summary: “One Night Only” director Will Gluck explains what happens at the end of the film with Owen and Allie.
story: Warning, spoilers ahead for the ending of “One Night Only.”
“One Night Only” is a rom-com unlike any other, so perhaps that’s why the ending may throw some viewers for a loop.

Set in a dystopian New York City where premarital sex is illegal, the film follows Owen (Callum Turner) and Allie (Monica Barbaro), two complete strangers who continue to run into each other on the one night a year that singles can get it on.

Owen, a pizza shop owner, has recently been dumped by his long-term girlfriend Malika (Maya Hawke), who wants to spend the “one night” with someone else. Heartbroken, he sets out to find someone to take his mind off her.

Allie is an aspiring singer who has stage fright but makes jingles for a living. She’s also looking for real love, not just a one night stand during the 12 hours that sex is legal. When Allie does set her sights on a certain someone, including rockstar Ezra Stone (Charlie Gillespie), it usually ends up in flames.
So as the clock is running out and both have multiple misses on finding someone for the night, Owen and Allie keep finding their way back to each other.
What Happens at the End of ‘One Night Only’?
After spending hours together, discussing their love lives and careers, Allie realizes that Owen might be the one. She runs over to his pizza shop in hope that she will find him there. She does.
The two once again bond as he makes a pizza and they enjoy the pie together. Just when it looks like they might choose each other, Malika asks to see Owen and he leaves for their apartment.
Malika tells Owen she regrets wanting to hook up with someone else, but as she’s apologizing he realizes he is in love with Allie.
He goes to Allie’s apartment to confess his love, but no luck. Owen then recalls Allie’s sentimental story about the red lighthouse under the George Washington Bridge. And that is where he finds her.
The two profess their love for each other and how they’d like to be together. And with the time to have sex almost up, they decide to not engage in intercourse and simply date.
Cut to a year later, they’re still dating and it’s that spicy day of the year.
Known for hit rom-coms like “Easy A” and “Anyone But You,” director Will Gluck tells TODAY.com he’s always trying to give viewers something they haven’t seen before.
“Even though it works out the way it’s supposed to, it’s not where we think it’s going to be,” Gluck says. “So anything that’s a little different is kind of refreshing.”
Why Don’t Owen and Allie Hook Up at the End of ‘One Night Only’?
So why, after 12 hours of running around NYC for their one night stand and falling in love, did Owen and Allie not go for it?
“Well, first of all, they didn’t have much time left, so practically it wouldn’t have been a very fun experience,” Gluck says. “It’d be very quick.”
In his eyes, the “most romantic” gesture at that moment had nothing to do with physical intimacy.
He says, “It’s just, ‘I really want to spend more time with you.’”

“My favorite line in the movie is when Owen says to (Allie), ‘I don’t want this moment to end,’ meaning the moment they’re in each other’s arms, talking,” he continues. “At that moment, Owen would rather spend the last eight minutes talking and being with her than having sex. He chose romance and love ... which I think is kind of cool.”

title: ‘Recess Therapy’ Host Julian Shapiro-Barnum Shares Off-Camera Reality of Working with Kids and Celebrities
summary: At 27, Julian Shapiro-Barnum is already many things: a TIME100 Creator, theatre graduate and the host of the child-interview Instagram series “Recess Therapy,” which made a kid go viral for loving corn.
story: At 27, Julian Shapiro-Barnum is already many things: a TIME100 Creator, theatre graduate and the host of the child-interview Instagram series “Recess Therapy,” which made a kid go viral for loving corn.

The Brooklyn native is also the creator of “Celebrity Substitute,” another internet series that brings celebrities like Tom Holland and Millie Bobby Brown to elementary classroom settings. (Most recently, a child left Holland speechless after outright asking him to confirm rumors of his marriage to Zendaya.) And some may also know Shapiro-Barnum as the guy trying to reinvent late-night for a digital world with his variety show, “Outside Tonight,” which premiered in June.
But on Aug. 4, Shapiro-Barnum appeared on TODAY to talk about something completely different: his first book.

In “How To Grow Up Without Becoming A Grown-Up: Big Lessons from Little Kids,” Shapiro-Barnum intentionally started over. He didn’t transcribe the previous thousands of interviews with kids he has collected over the years with “Recess Therapy.” Instead, he had all new conversations, some with recurring characters from his series like 7-year-old Miles, and some with new kids, full of accidental wisdom for adults.
TODAY.com caught up with Shapiro-Barnum to chat about his debut book, his career online and efforts to grow a new audience beyond “Recess Therapy.”

I’m trying to think of things I can share ... let me think. They can be very rude. Kids have snapped at me to ask for things, like with their fingers. They’ll be like, “Get me that,” and I’ll be like, “Excuse me?” And I don’t stand for it, I say no.
You learn a lot about people’s parents very quickly.

Reps and agents are so much harder. Parents are pretty easy. People always think that parents are going to be like show parents, but not in New York. Parents are really chill and awesome. And then every once and awhile, we’ll get a parent who wants their kid to be a star, and I don’t mess with that. To me, it’s not what the show is about. It’s about them just being a kid, having fun. But no, everyone’s teams are difficult. And I would say that with my full chest. It’s you know, whatever, I don’t need to caveat it. People need to be taken care of.

I had only done the kid thing online and was feeling like I was limiting me entirely. Like, I couldn’t even post my life, me and my friends, or, I just felt a little bit like I could only post stuff that was about me and kids. There was a moment where I was, like, I cannot even post myself being inside. I was just that stressed about it. Maybe it was connected to anxiety. I don’t know how rational it was, is what I’m saying. And then, with “Outside Tonight,” I needed to free myself from that.

So, before we started the show, we did this social series that I built with my friend Bailey Whitehead, who ran socials for the show, where we just went completely in the other direction, where I did all this ridiculous stuff that we purposely made crazier than the actual show was going to be, as a way to test the waters and see what I could get away with.

The character we created for that was me, but super bad at being inappropriate. It was me trying to break out of my shell, but being awful at it, which felt in a lot of ways true. I don’t feel like my actual self is that different than the version of myself that I am when I work with kids. But I felt like I wanted to be a little bit more authentic to who I am off camera so that it wasn’t like “Kid Julian” online and then “Real Julian.” I wanted to meet in the middle.

I’m always worried about everything. A lot of the parents of kids were really supportive of me. A lot of the parents watch it and are really supportive, and I’m sure it upsets some people, somewhere. To me, I’d rather be myself and make things that I want to make, then fit some box that I’ve put myself in. I’d rather like set myself back and make what I want to be making.

I think my whole theory of late night and digital and the way they play together is that digital shows are this fractured late night show. Late night was a variety show. Internet shows took those pieces of variety and expanded upon each piece individually. I was like, maybe you put them back together now, using what we learned from the breaking them apart. We unstitched them.

We went, “Recess Therapy,” “Subway Takes,” “Track Star,” “Hot and Single” — all these shows work on their own. What if we then took all that and put it back together? People would still engage and find it interesting, but we’re using the findings of pure short form digital to reintegrate them into long form. We were hoping that would engage people. And maybe it did, I don’t know. We’ll see.

No, and I get a lot of flack for that sometimes from maybe my mom. She’s, like, “Think more about it.” But I think I just make something that I want to make. And I hope other people love it. I think if I make something I want to make, I hope that I’m enough of a demographic.
I don’t know. My mom says it’s too niche. I think it’s not niche. I said to my mom, “Is ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show’ too niche?” That did pretty well. I said, “Is John Waters too niche?”

So initially, I went, well this is only six weeks old, so it’s a conversation that’s had in the household a lot. I don’t live with my mom, but we were on the phone this weekend. This is a conversation I’m having right now, and it’s interesting.

I think with Season 1 of “Outside Tonight,” we had to make it as is, on the budget and the timeline that we had. I’d worked on funding and building that show for two years, and then we had four weeks to make it, because that’s what we could afford to do. Now we’re looking at Season 2, and we learned everything, and we want to change everything. And we’re really proud of what we did, but it’s, like, we gathered a boatload of information, and we’re metabolizing that data.

The most helpful thing we could have done for the show was to make the show. And now we’re meeting and talking and reshaping and retooling. That’s now the exciting part. Because at first it was just like, will this work? Can I even do it? And we did it. And now it’s like, how can we do it better?

Writing is hard. I wrote it myself. I think what I want to say about the book that maybe I haven’t said before is that you can watch “Recess Therapy.” But with the book, I was like, how can I give something that isn’t online already?

I tried to offer a lot of stories and insights and quotes. I did all new interviews for the book and really tried to give people who like what I do, something that isn’t anywhere else. I feel like sometimes I’ve seen people who have an online thing that they translate to a book, just kind of rehashing what is on the internet, and I was like, let me do something that’s fresh.

title: Mark Ruffalo’s Son Keen Didn’t Plan on Acting. Here’s What Changed His Mind
summary: Keen Ruffalo, son of four-time Oscar-nominated actor Mark Ruffalo, currently stars alongside Ella Rubin in Prime Video’s teen drama series, “Sterling Point.” The 25-year-old stopped by TODAY on Aug. 7 and opened up about finding acting amid a period of burnout and isolation.
story: Keen Ruffalo didn’t always plan to go into acting. But one particular experience inspired him to follow in his famous dad’s footsteps.

Keen Ruffalo, son of four-time Oscar-nominated actor Mark Ruffalo, currently stars alongside Ella Rubin in Prime Video’s teen drama series, “Sterling Point.” The 25-year-old stopped by TODAY on Aug. 7 and opened up about finding acting amid a period of burnout and isolation.
Keen Ruffalo, who initially went to college for fashion design before dropping out, explained that he decided to make a life change amid the Covid-19 pandemic.

“I got the Covid depression, as many people did, and I needed a change, and I was lost at the time,” Keen Ruffalo told TODAY. “I saw that acting made my dad so happy, and I was like, ‘Listen, I need to try something new.’”

Keen Ruffalo’s dad, of course, has long been a critically acclaimed actor whose career spans nearly four decades. Mark Ruffalo’s acting chops have earned him two Primetime Emmy Awards, a Golden Globe Award and three Screen Actors Guild Awards among many other accolades.

But Keen Ruffalo is charting his own path. In “Sterling Point,” he plays Connor who, along with his fellow adopted twin Annie, played by Rubin, uncovers a slew of family secrets previously concealed by their relatives.
While Keen Ruffalo is a pro on set now, his father, though supportive, wasn’t initially sure about his decision to pivot into acting.
“He was like, ‘You sure you want to do this?’” Keen Ruffalo said, imitating his dad.

At the time, Keen Ruffalo did not have much experience in the acting world. But he did make an appearance as an extra in “Thor: Ragnarok,” the 2017 Marvel film that starred his father as the green and mighty Hulk.  The 25-year-old’s formal acting career started off with 100 auditions before he got a gig, he said in an interview with Cultured Magazine.
To nail the “Sterling Point” character of Connor — the voice of sarcasm and wittiness amid an extremely complex period of change in his family — Keen Ruffalo said he leaned into his instincts.
“I improvised quite a lot of it,” he said of the comedic banter throughout the show.
Keen Ruffalo added that “pretty much in any scene where there’s a kind of comedic effect, I do it clean lines for a few times, and then we kind of just had fun with it.”
His antics also led to a reshoot after he made the director of photography laugh during the first take of a bathtub scene, he told TODAY.
Ruffalo will also be in the upcoming Green Day-produced film “Nimrods,” starring Mason Thames and McKenna Grace, out in theaters on Aug. 14.

title: What Happened to Anthony Bourdain After ‘Tony’? A Look Back at His Life and Death
summary: Read what beloved chef Anthony Bourdain shared about his personal life and what we know about his tragic death at the age of 61 in 2018.
story: If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or go to 988lifeline.org, to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.
If the Anthony Bourdain biopic “Tony” was the equivalent of a 12-course menu, it would be the amuse-bouche in the story of the world-renowned chef’s life.

“Tony,” out Aug. 7, shows actor Dominic Sessa taking on the role of Bourdain before the accolades and fame. In the coming-of-age drama, which has received overwhelmingly positive reviews from critics, Sessa’s Bourdain is 19 years old and dreams of becoming a writer. But on a whim, he decides to travel to Cape Cod for a summer and finds himself working in a restaurant headed by a worldly chef (Antonio Banderas).

The film portrays a version of Bourdain that fans might not find recognizable if they discovered him through his Emmy-winning television shows “No Reservations” and “Parts Unknown,” or his bestseller “Kitchen Confidential.”

Bourdain, who went on to become a student at the Culinary Institute of America after that one pivotal summer and eventually a James Beard award-winning chef, opened up throughout his career about his unconventional rise to fame and the invaluable lessons he learned after experiencing cultures and cuisines all over the world.
Read what Bourdain said about his personal life, what his love for food taught him and what we know about his tragic death at the age of 61 in 2018, below.
What Did Anthony Bourdain Say About His Success?

Bourdain graduated from the Culinary Institute of America, or the CIA, in 1978, kickstarting a decades-long career working in kitchens. However, he didn’t become the media personality that fans came to adore until “Kitchen Confidential,” a behind-the-scenes look at the culinary world and restaurant business, was published in 2000 when he was about 44.
When he spoke with Willie Geist on Sunday TODAY in 2016, the chef shared how the book came about.

“I wrote an article. My mom actually said you should send it to the New Yorker,” he recalled. “I mean the next day I got a call saying, you know, ‘We’ll give you 50 grand to write a book.’ I’m no dummy. I’m dunking French fries at age 44, and I’ll write the damn book.”
In addition to his stories about the different kitchens he worked in, Bourdain also discussed his struggles with drug addiction in the book.
The popularity of “Kitchen Confidential” spawned television offers.
While speaking about his shows, he told Geist, “I’m curious about the world and if there are manageable risks in return for satisfying my curiosity about a place. I’m willing.”

“The kind of questions we are asking are, ‘What does your soul crave at 2 o’ clock in the morning?’ When you got a little bit of a buzz,” Bourdain said of his show. “More often than not, that goes right to the heart of the culture — that beloved, local favorite that tells you a lot about the place and about the people.
When he wasn’t busy traveling the world and visiting new spots, he enjoyed spending time cooking at home with his family, including daughter Ariane Bourdain.
He described his daughter, who was 7 years old at the time, as a “brutal” critic.
“I cannot get anything past her. It’s like, ‘No, Daddy, it’s too salty,’” he said, sharing some of her feedback. “Secretly, I know. Yeah, she caught me every time.”
He revealed that his daughter inspired 2016’s “Appetites: A Cookbook,” which became his final cookbook published before his death.
What Did Anthony Bourdain Say About His Love for Food?

Bourdain’s success also stemmed from his public persona as a chef who rejected the idea that the best food had to be cooked in an expensive, Michelin-starred restaurant. When he stepped into a Waffle House for the first time in 2015 and grabbed breakfast, he raved about the meal.

“It is indeed marvelous. An irony-free zone where everything is beautiful and nothing hurts,” he said about the chain in a “Anthony Bourdain: Parts Unknown” episode. After digging into his pecan waffles, he praised, “This is better than The French Laundry, man!”
The diner meal was a reflection of Bourdain’s message: good food can come from anywhere and bring people together.
In an interview with PBS News in 2016 about the power of food, he voiced that mindset. “Food may not be the answer to world peace, but it’s a start,” he said.
How Did Anthony Bourdain Die?
Bourdain died on June 8, 2018 at 61 while working on an episode of “Parts Unknown” in Strasbourg, France.
The network reported that his cause of death was suicide.

“It is with extraordinary sadness we can confirm the death of our friend and colleague, Anthony Bourdain. His love of great adventure, new friends, fine food and drink and the remarkable stories of the world made him a unique storyteller,” CNN said in a statement. “His talents never ceased to amaze us and we will miss him very much. Our thoughts and prayers are with his daughter and family at this incredibly difficult time.”
NBC News confirmed that French police found Bourdain’s body in his room at the Chambard Hotel. CNN reported that fellow esteemed chef and close friend Eric Ripert was the one who found him.
Ripert and many leading figures in the culinary world, from Gordon Ramsay to Nigella Lawson and Marcus Samuelsson, paid tribute to the late chef following reports of his death.
In a statement to NBC News, Ripert described Bourdain as “an exceptional human being, so inspiring and generous.”
“One of the great storytellers of our time who connected with so many,” he continued, “I wish him peace.”
A year after his passing, Ripert and chef José Andrés announced the first #BourdainDay, celebrating Bourdain’s impact around the world.
On the two-year anniversary of his death, fans honored him with countless social media posts highlighting his lasting legacy.

title: ‘Teenage Sex and Death At Camp Miasma’ Isn’t Supposed to Make Perfect Sense
summary: Jane Schoenbrun and Hannah Einbinder unpack the movie Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, including the ending.
story: Just from the synopsis of “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” it’s clear that this isn’t your typical slasher film. In fact, it aims to deconstruct everything audiences understand about the genre.

“Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” from writer and director Jane Schoenbrun, follows Kris (Hannah Einbinder), a young queer filmmaker fresh off the film festival success of her first project, which took the cult-classic “Psycho” and reimagined it through the perspective of Marion’s shower curtain.

When Kris is given the opportunity to revitalize the exhausted “zombie IP” of the “Camp Miasma” horror franchise, she visits retired actress Billy Preston (Gillian Anderson), who lives at the abandoned sleepaway camp where the franchise was filmed, to convince her to reprise her role as the original film’s “final girl.”

Kris has some big ideas about the gender and sexuality dynamics perpetuated in the roles within horror tropes. As she and Billy grow closer, and their relationship becomes steamy, she discovers her thoughts are not all that abstract.
“It’s a movie about sex,” Schoenbrun tells TODAY.com — and they mean that on a meta level. “I, as a filmmaker, am seducing you into enjoying the film and engaging with it emotionally.”
As lines between what’s fictional and real are blurred, Schoenbrun knows you might have questions. They say the questions are the point.
“If the choice is between somebody feeling something or understanding something in film, always feeling should win,” Schoenbrun says.

“Some people will be like, ‘That was so f---- confusing, I’m annoyed,’ and some people will want to ask questions or talk to it a little bit, and some of those people who ask questions and talk to it, it’ll lead them somewhere that’s fruitful.”
When asked if audiences are supposed to fully understand the line between fact and fiction throughout the film, Schoenbrun wears a knowing smile.
“David Lynch answer?” Einbinder convenes with her director.
“You’re supposed to feel it, baby!” Schoenbrun says.
Like Lynch, the mind behind genre classics like “Mulholland Drive” and “Lost Highway,” Schoenbrun’s films, notably “I Saw The TV Glow,” use form to play with fractured, subjective realities.

“I’m trying to talk about things that are not easy to express in a three-act narrative form, so I’m using three-act narrative form as scaffolding, but then I’m complicating the language that we’re used to in movies in various ways,” Schoenbrun says.

Einbinder, who first graced screens in her breakout role as Ava Daniels in the Emmy-award-winning HBO Max series “Hacks,” says that while her characters Ava and Kris are similar in some ways, elements like wardrobe, setting and working with Schoenbrun allowed her to create a distinct character.

“So much of what I understood Kris to be on the page, and what I hope I communicated, was a person who was a little headier and more neurotic, and less sure of themselves, and who felt that underlying discomfort,” Einbinder tells TODAY.com.
Einbinder hopes that, regardless of age, “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” challenges audiences to examine their own comfort levels.

She hopes that “if folks have not examined what the film is trying to contend with, that they do, that they start to ask, ‘Is this true for me? How true is it? In what ways is it true? Do I feel OK in my body? Have I ever been present? Have I ever been fully comfortable? Why have I not?’”
As for the ending? Don’t worry too much about it.
“That’s a complicated and strange thing that I don’t know if anyone fully understands, so be with the mystery,” Schoenbrun says.

title: With ‘One Night Only,’ Director Will Gluck Tried to Give the People What They Want – Even if It’s ‘Cliche’
summary: “One Night Only” director Will Gluck shares what the key is to making a successful rom-com and explains that unexpected ending.
story: Warning: Spoilers ahead for “One Night Only”
There’s a scene in “One Night Only,” the new romantic comedy starring Callum Turner and Monica Barbaro, where their characters, Owen and Allie, have a flirty exchange in the back of a car.
“You’re cute when you’re nervous,” Owen tells Allie after running around New York City in search for the perfect one night stand.
“I’m not nervous,” she quips, as Owen smoothly replies, “So then you’re just cute.”
The brief and subtle interaction could be considered a cheesy pickup line, yet for Allie and Owen, giddiness ensues.
And that’s because “One Night Only” director Will Gluck knew viewers would be invested in the two stars, their attraction for each other — and the unorthodox plot of the film.

Set in a fictionalized and modern New York City, “One Night Only,” written by Travis Braun, is a dystopian rom-com where premarital sex is illegal. But for one night only, unmarried couples and single people have 12 hours to get it on. So when Owen and Allie — two complete strangers in the search for that special someone — keep running into each other, viewers wonder: could they be the one for each other?

“Whenever I do a movie, and you decide who’s going to be in it — or you’re lucky enough for them to say yes to it — then I redo the script for them,” Gluck, the director behind “Easy A” and “Anyone But You,” tells TODAY.com. “By the time we get to the set and actually start shooting after rehearsals and all the rewrites, the movie is about them.”

Callum is a British actor known for “Masters of the Air,” the “Fantastic Beasts” franchise and “Eternity” (not to mention his recent wedding to Dua Lipa). Then there’s Barbaro, whose credits include “Top Gun: Maverick,” “At Midnight” and “A Complete Unknown,” which earned her an Oscar nomination for her portrayal of Joan Baez.
Both having dabbled in the rom-com genre, and plenty of other action-packed films, Gluck made sure to craft “One Night Only” around their strengths.

“Like for Monica, I (said), ‘Let’s make music.’ So I wrote all the stuff about all her songs,” Gluck says. Allie is a singer who has stage fright and creates jingles for a living. Barbaro, on her end, sings as well. “It’s all about what they’re comfortable doing.”
Gluck adds that tailoring a script to the stars is key to making a rom-com succeed, but there’s also something more.
“Because for romance, it’s all about: Do you want to spend time watching these two people together?” he says. “And I don’t mean in bed, I mean when they’re talking with each other.”

“So you want the personality to come out,” he continues. “I think good chemistry means that each other enjoys each other’s personality, and when you have someone who is enjoying each other’s personality, that’s really fun to watch.”
From the moment that Owen and Allie meet, Gluck knew “there’s a spark.”
“But that’s kind of a fake spark,” he adds.

He specifically points out a scene where he “couldn’t stop watching” the two and knew they were perfect for each other. It was when they are in the bodega trying to get money at the ATM that Gluck says the characters “start having real conversations with each other.”

“Because at that point, they don’t want anything from each other sexually, romantically, at all,” he explains. “It’s just two people talking ... they’re just going about their own business, and yet they’re kind of flirting with words.”
Among Gluck’s pleasures when crafting a rom-com is writing and watching characters that make you wish they spoke that way to you.

“That one scene when they really go at each other, kind of giving each other the business — you know that there’s something underneath that,” he says. “And that was the moment for me, even in filming that moment, I said, ‘Oh, you want to see these two together.’”

There’s another element to making a romantic comedy strike gold with viewers, Gluck notes. While he often rails against cliché moments in rom-coms, like a meet-cute, opposites attract and other known storylines, he understands they’re cliché for a reason.
“I think people in life want those moments,” he says, explaining, “What they really mean is, ‘Oh boy, I want that moment in my life.’ So sometimes you have to give them that.”
He says that as a filmmaker, “You don’t set out to make a trope.” But when the chase is on, “You try really hard to make it feel different than other ones but ... you still want them to connect.”

While he wants to get to the happily ever after, he attempts to do it in a way viewers haven’t seen before. “And in this movie... Even though it works out the way it’s supposed to, it’s not where we think it’s going to be. So anything that’s a little different is kind of refreshing.”

title: Kylie Kelce Shares the Moment That Made Jason So Emotional at Travis and Taylor Swift’s Wedding
summary: Kylie Kelce responded to husband Jason Kelce’s comments that he cried more at brother Travis Kelce’s wedding than his own — and there’s an extra special reason.
story: There’s a reason why Jason Kelce was extra emotional at his brother Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift’s wedding — and the answer is really sweet.
Kylie Kelce shared some insight after her husband recently shared that he “probably cried more at this wedding than I cried at my own wedding, which probably is not acceptable.”

Jason Kelce served as his brother’s best man during the star-studded July 3 wedding at Madison Square Garden. During his chat with Philadelphia radio station 94WIP in July, Jason Kelce jokingly added that wife Kylie Kelce was most likely “not happy” he cried more at this wedding than his own.
But how did Kylie Kelce really feel? She answered that very question and provided more details about the celebration on the Aug. 6 episode of her “Not Gonna Lie With Kylie Kelce” podcast.

“Don’t worry, my husband cried plenty at his own wedding, regardless of what his comments were recently,” she said, before joking about how she would have reacted if she didn’t get the reaction she wanted from her husband.

“Guys, think about this. First of all, there was a moment in time where I said if he didn’t tear up when I started walking down the aisle, I would go back and start again, knowing that someone would have obviously punched him in the nose between me restarting,” she said. “And he would have been crying when I walked down the aisle.”
On a serious note, however, she told listeners to “consider the context” of what the retired Eagles player said because there’s more to the story.
“Obviously, my husband cried during our wedding. He did,” she said. “I think that goes without being said because he’s cried a couple other places because he feels his emotions, OK.”
She continued by adding that “more importantly,” Jason Kelce cried at his brother’s wedding “for many reasons.”

“It was touching. It was very loving to see all of the things that were happening,” she said, pointing out one very specific moment during Travis Kelce and Swift’s wedding. “But take this into consideration, because no one’s thinking about this, think about getting to watch your four daughters be flower girls. OK? That’s all the information you get.”
Jason Kelce previously confirmed in an interview that his little girls — Wyatt, 6, Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 1 — were flower girls.
“They’re beautiful, they’re incredible personalities and Travis and Taylor love them,” he told the Reno Gazette Journal.
Kylie Kelce echoed the sentiments, sharing on her podcast that it was also a sentimental moment for her.
“It was emotional and he was not the only adult crying in our family,” she said, adding that she was also “guilty.” “Mmkay? Come on. Be for real.”
She concluded her wedding talk by quipping that she has given her husband “s--- about (his comments), and yes, I will continue to, ‘cause that is my right as his wife.”

title: ‘My Life with the Walter Boys’ Season 3 Ending Explained
summary: What happens at the end of Season 3 of My Life with the Walter Boys? Read a recap of Season 3 and find out what’s next.
story: Warning: Spoilers ahead for Season 3 of “My Life with the Walter Boys.”
If you thought Season 2 of “My Life with the Walter Boys” ended with a bang, just wait until you watch Season 3.

The hit Netflix series returned with 10 new episodes Aug. 6 and continued its streak of leaving viewers on the edge of their seats with an action-packed season finale. Luckily, the show has already been renewed for Season 4.

Season 3 finds Jackie (Nikki Rodriguez) exploring her chemistry with Cole (Noah LaLonde). After starting off slow, their romance quickly heats up and they finally seem to be on the right track, especially when Alex (Ashby Gentry) begins to make peace with the end of his relationship with Jackie.

Then, a newcomer shows up in town: Eliot (Naveen Paddock), Jackie’s childhood friend from New York. Eliot represents everything from Jackie’s life before moving to Colorado — ambition, hustle culture and a fast-paced life — and her uncle Richard wants to make sure Jackie hasn’t let the slow pace of Colorado life (or her romance with notorious bad boy Cole) impact her future goals.

Later on in the season, Eliot and Richard get into Cole’s head and convince him that he’s holding Jackie back and having a negative influence on her. Worried that Jackie truly is better off without him, Cole breaks up with her in cruel fashion. Alas, he’s still in love with her, and several members of his family urge him to make things right.
All the teenage drama comes to a head in the Season 3 finale, which will leave you eagerly counting down the days until Season 4 arrives.
Jackie’s Community Center Opens

All season long, Jackie worked to create a community space for teens in Silver Falls. With one week left until the opening event, she runs into some major issues when a pipe bursts in the building, causing a bunch of damage to the space.

Jackie learns that it could take several weeks to repair, and she doesn’t want to postpone the event. However, she quickly discovers that making the repairs in a timely manner is going to be quite expensive.

When Cole hears the news, he visits Jackie’s uncle Richard and asks him if there’s anything he can do to expedite the repairs process. Richard teams up with George (Marc Blucas) and the Walter family to make sure the space is ready in time for the event. Still, Jackie is unaware that Cole had orchestrated the quick turnaround.
At the event, Alex tells Jackie that Cole spoke with Richard, offered to pay the contractors himself and enlisted help from his coworkers at the auto shop he works at to help with the repairs.

Jackie is confused and wonders why Cole would go to such lengths to help when he broke up with her. Alex tells her it’s “complicated” and Eliot interrupts their conversation before he can divulge any additional information.
Nathan Prepares to Leave Town for an Exciting Opportunity
After auditioning for a European band tour, Nathan (Corey Fogelmanis) learns that he got the spot. Even better, his parents agreed to let him go.

When Nathan tells Alex the big news, Alex notes that Nathan doesn’t seem super excited. Nathan then explains that he’s eager to do something to find out who he is and what he wants. At the same time, he’s nervous that the timing isn’t right, especially since their dad is recovering from his stroke and Will (Johnny Link) and Haley (Zoë Soul) just left town.
Alex encourages Nathan to pursue his dreams. Nathan breaks the news to his ex, Skylar (Jaylan Evans), who says he will miss him while he’s gone.
Alex Renews His Passion for Horses After Quitting the Rodeo

After earning a saddle bronc riding sponsorship in Season 2, Alex gets more involved with his team in Season 3. A lot of the guys are significantly older and they pressure him to drink and get a tattoo.

When one of the riders offers Alex pain pills to cope with the injuries they sustain while riding, Alex ends up inadvertently reporting him during a frustrating rant about the team’s complicated dynamics.

Alex ends up walking about from saddle bronc riding, but his mom Katherine (Sarah Rafferty) ends up offering him another way to connect with horses when she brings an injured wild horse back to the Walter family ranch.

While talking with George, Katherine says she figured Alex needed something to shift his attention to after stepping away from the rodeo. Plus, she doesn’t want him to leave the ranch like Nathan and Will.
Dylan Asks Alex to Stay Away from Kiley
Alex’s best friend Kiley (Mya Lowe) has always had a thing for him, but she started dating Dylan (Kolton Stewart) in Season 2 and their relationship is going strong in Season 3.

Kiley likes to keep her home life private since her grandmother has a drinking problem, so she hesitates to invite Dylan over as their relationship progresses. But when Dylan finds out that Alex regularly spends time at Kiley’s house with her grandmother, Dylan grows jealous of their friendship.

Throughout the season, Alex tagged along with the couple on several outings. Alex begins to notice his own feelings for Kiley and he kisses her one day. They both agree that it shouldn’t have happened since she’s with Dylan. Still, Alex can’t stop thinking about it and he’s worried since Kiley is avoiding him after the kiss.

In the season finale, Dylan asks Alex to keep his distance from Kiley and he agrees to do so. However, he later visits Kiley at home, seemingly to declare his feelings for her, and he’s crushed to see that she invited Dylan over, signaling that their relationship is going better than ever.
Danny Gets Into Carnegie Mellon University

Danny (Connor Stanhope) and Erin’s (Alisha Newton) relationship has been going strong in Season 3. After he drunkenly proposed to her one night, things got a bit awkward, but they later agreed that they both want to get married at some point.
In the Season 3 finale, Danny announces that he was accepted to Carnegie Mellon University. Erin is thrilled for him, especially since he was crushed when he wasn’t accepted to The Juilliard School.

Erin plans to stay in Colorado for college, so Danny is understandably concerned about attending a school across the country. However, Erin convinces him that they’ll make the whole long distance thing work.
They still have some time to figure things out, but Danny reassures Erin that his dream is being wherever Erin is.
Jackie and Eliot Kiss

Ever since Eliot arrived in Silver Falls, he’s been trying his hardest to steal Jackie from Cole. After Jackie and Cole break up, Eliot tries to make a move when Jackie asks if he wants to come to the community center opening event with him. When he asks if it’s a date, she says she’s not ready to date yet after her breakup, but he still agrees to go with her.
At the event, Jackie pulls Eliot onto the dance floor. In the last second of the season finale, he moves in for a kiss and the scene ends.
Cole Gets Into a Scary Car Accident
Cole has always been into cars, but he begins racing them in Season 3 after meeting a drag racer named Mac (Chad Rook).
In the season finale, Cole nails one of his races and is preparing for another round when he decides that he’s waited long enough to tell Jackie why he broke up with her.
Cole ends up leaving before his other race, much to the dismay of his competitor, who was relying on the race to give him the opportunity to either qualify for another race or earn some money.

Cole’s competitor follows him home and starts driving aggressively behind him. Cole does his best to keep his distance, but his rival dries him off the road and Cole’s car ends up flipping over multiple times, leaving viewers wondering if he could’ve survived the accident.

title: Tan France Responds to Karamo Brown Saying ‘Queer Eye’ Was a ‘Nightmare’
summary: Tan France shared his reaction to fellow “Queer Eye” castmate Karamo Brown’s assertion there was a toxic culture on the set of the show before its conclusion after 10 seasons earlier this year.
story: Tan France shared his reaction to fellow “Queer Eye” castmate Karamo Brown’s assertion that there was a toxic culture on the set of the show before its conclusion after 10 seasons earlier this year.

In a People magazine cover story in June titled “Surviving My Reality TV Nightmare,” Brown said he clashed with some of his costars, describing bullying from executives and production members and opened up about relapsing in 2018 during the third season of the show.
France, 43, spoke with Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones on TODAY Aug. 6 about Brown’s comments.

“First of all, I’m sad that was the experience that he felt like it was a nightmare, as I said it was a dream for me,” France said. “I couldn’t believe it. And so for me, I look back thinking, gosh, we did what I think was incredible work and had a phenomenal experience.
“I’m so proud of what we did, and all I want is for the audience to remember that. I want them to know that it was so real for me on that show. Every experience that I had was special,” he added.
The Netflix show released its 10th and final season in January. The show’s producers disputed Brown’s claims about the environment on set.

“We strongly disagree with any characterization that concerns raised during the production of ‘Queer Eye’ were ignored, dismissed or allowed to continue unchecked,” the show’s production company, ITV America and Scout Productions, told People at the time.
Brown was set to attend a Jan. 20 interview on TODAY with France and castmates Antoni Porowski, Jonathan Van Ness and Jeremiah Brent to promote the show, but he canceled last-minute.
He explained his absence in a June 23 appearance on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle.

“One of the things that I’ve been teaching people right now is that two things can be true at once,” he said. “‘Queer Eye’ was one of the most amazing shows — the impact that it had culturally for 10 years and what we were able to do. One of the things I’ll say about my cast, no matter what we were going through, we always made sure that the hero was No. 1, that the person we were helping, the crew worked so hard.

“But on the flip side, you can also have a bad experience,” he continued. “And you can also feel as if you’re not being protected and things are not going well. So while I loved what we did, it didn’t mean that I loved what was happening to me.”
During the group interview without Brown on TODAY in January, one of his costars remarked on his absence.
“I think (we’re) definitely a little surprised, but at the same time, like, look, we’re so sorry that he’s not here,” Porowski said.
France made it clear in his Aug. 6 appearance on TODAY that he enjoyed his time on the show, which followed a “Fab Five” team of gay professionals giving lifestyle makeovers to guests.

“Now I look back thinking, gosh, we won loads of Emmys, we were nominated for an Emmy again this season, that’s wild after all those years to still feel so positively about your work,” he said. “If they wanted to do another 10 seasons, I’m like yeah, it was the greatest gift of my life.”

The British-born fashion designer also said he’s grateful to have seen so much of the U.S. thanks to his time on “Queer Eye.” He’s currently moving from Salt Lake City to New York City with his husband and two children.

“I am the luckiest man in the world,” he said. “I got to do, in my opinion, the best job in the world with some of the greatest people that you could ever meet. I got to see America through a lens that no one else really gets to.”

title: ‘Freaky Friday’ Turns 23: Watch Lindsay Lohan Praise Jamie Lee Curtis on TODAY in 2004
summary: While appearing on TODAY in 2004, Lindsay Lohan spoke about her relationship with “Freaky Friday” co-star Jamie Lee Curtis.
story: Welcome inside the TODAY Vault, where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Lindsay Lohan on TODAY on April 23, 2004, talking about her new film “Mean Girls,” as well as the success of “Freaky Friday,” which came out the year before.

At age 17, Lindsay Lohan was already a well-established star when she visited TODAY on April 23, 2004, plugging a little movie called “Mean Girls” that would go on to become a cultural phenomenon. While she was on hand to talk about that flick, she did take some time to gush about “Freaky Friday,” which had come out less than a year earlier on Aug. 6, 2003.

“Freaky Friday,” which also featured Jamie Lee Curtis, wound up earning more than $100 million and spurred a 2025 sequel. It also cemented Lohan’s place among the hottest young celebrities of the early and mid-2000s.
What Did Lindsay Lohan Say About Jamie Lee Curtis?

During her chat with Katie Couric, the former TODAY anchor ran down some of the films Lohan had made by that point in her career, including “The Parent Trap,” “Confessions of a Teenage Drama Queen” and “Freaky Friday.”
“You got a lot of great reviews for ‘Freaky Friday,’ particularly,” Couric told her before asking if she enjoyed starring alongside Curtis in the hit film.
“I had a great time working with her,” she said. “She was so sweet. She’s really down to earth. She’s so much fun on set.”
Lindsay Lohan Looked at Jamie Lee Curtis As a Mentor
In Curtis, Lohan saw more than just a co-star — she saw someone who could guide her and share her wisdom.
“We talk all the time. She’s kind of like a second parent. It’s nice to have that. She’s really sweet,” Lohan said.
The two stars would continue their close friendship and admiration for each other over the years.
How Did Lindsay Lohan Launch an Acting Career?

Lohan was a show business veteran by the time she was on TODAY in 2004, but she was not that far removed from getting her start. She recounted working as a model when she was 5 before moving into acting.
“When I was, like, 7, I did my first commercial. I just started going out on commercials, just because I really enjoyed it, and I was comfortable in front of the cameras and stuff,” she said.
However, there was a point when Lohan was ready to give up.
“And I didn’t get anything. And I was like, ‘Mom, if I don’t get this commercial today, then I’m never doing this again.’ And I actually got that commercial that day.”
During her 2004 TODAY interview, she also touched on working on her music career.

title: Perez Hilton’s Family Confirms He ‘Is Able To Communicate’ After Reports He Livestreamed Self-Harm
summary: Perez Hilton’s family shared a statement after police responded to the celebrity blogger’s home in Miami following a livestream that was flagged in which he allegedly engaged in self-harm.
story: This story discusses self-harm. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or go to 988lifeline.org, to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.
Perez Hilton’s family is speaking out after police responded to the celebrity blogger’s home in Miami following a livestream in which he allegedly engaged in self-harm.
In the latest statement posted Aug. 5 on Hilton’s website, the blogger’s family and team shared an update.

“We have also been able to confirm that Perez is able to communicate, which has given our family hope,” they said in the statement. “We respectfully ask for your continued prayers, understanding, and grace as Perez continues to recover.”
The family also described the situation as “incredibly difficult and emotional.”

“This has been incredibly difficult and emotional for us, made even harder because very little information has been made available to our family,” they said in the statement. “While we continue to wait for further updates, we remain hopeful.”
Earlier that day, they had shared in a separate statement that Hilton was receiving medical care.

The updates comes after reports of “someone who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media” the night before, a Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office spokesperson told NBC News. The person was “safely recovered,” the sheriff’s office said. Police did not identify Hilton by name.

“Many of you have reached out with concern for Perez,” said the initial statement, signed “The Perez Hilton Team and Family.” “We are incredibly grateful for the overwhelming outpouring of love, support, and prayers.”
The family added that their “focus right now is on his well-being.”
“We kindly ask that you respect Perez’s privacy, as well as the privacy of his family, during this difficult time,” the statement said.

The livestream was posted to TikTok before the platform pulled the video. It appeared to show Hilton, covered in blood and holding a knife with signs of injuries. Concerned viewers commented on the livestream, asking for his contact information and offering to call for help.

According to a TikTok U.S. spokesperson, the social media platform’s automated moderator systems flagged the livestream within minutes. Then, the U.S. moderation team reviewed it and law enforcement was alerted.

The content violated the platform’s community guidelines, the spokesperson added. According to TikTok’s mental and behavioral health policies, the platform allows individuals to “discuss emotionally complex topics in a supportive way without increasing the risk of harm.”
“We don’t allow showing, promoting, or sharing plans for suicide or self-harm,” the guidelines say.

Footage from Hilton’s neighborhood, taken by NBC South Florida, showed multiple police vehicles in the area. Cameras from the local NBC affiliate showed paramedics transporting a man into an ambulance and driving away.
The police spokesperson said in a statement that family members of the individual that they recovered have been contacted.
“Deputies quickly located the individual’s residence, where they spoke with family members on scene, and confirmed he was alone inside,” the spokesperson said.

Hilton, who was born Mario Lavandeira, has three children — Mario III, Mia and Mayte Amor— all born via surrogacy. In a 2017 essay published on HuffPost, Hilton also mentioned that his mother lives with the family.
“Not many families are able to have that opportunity,” he wrote in the essay. “That difference makes us special and awesome, to me and us.”
In June, Hilton shared in a video that he and his family had moved back to Miami after a three-and-a-half-year-long stint in Las Vegas.
Hilton’s family and team said in their latest statement that they will continue to share updates “as we receive confirmed information and are able to do so.”
“Again, thank you, truly, for all your support and compassion,” the statement said. “We are so grateful.”

Chris Booker, who co-hosts “The Perez Hilton Podcast with Chris Booker” with the blogger, released a statement on Aug. 5 as well in response to the news. Booker said that he has only spoken “briefly” with Hilton’s family, who are struggling with getting updates themselves due to the security measures in place at the hospital. He reiterated that any official updates will appear on Hilton’s website.
“I am so profoundly sad for Perez and his family and what they’re all going through,” Booker said in the statement, shared on social media. “It’s truly unimaginable.”
Booker also said that the podcast is up in the air “as our collective focus is on his health.”
“I certainly hope to continue them with my friend when the time is right,” Booker wrote, adding that the support from fans has been “resounding.”
“He is very loved,” Booker wrote. “I can only hope that he feels it.”
Hilton’s agent Dante Rusciolelli, CEO and talent manager at Golden Arts Entertainment, also shared a statement on Aug. 5, asking the public to honor Hilton’s privacy as he receives care.
“At this time, we do not have any additional confirmed information to share regarding Perez Hilton’s condition,” the statement said.
Verified updates will come “directly from Dante Rusciolelli at Golden Artists Entertainment,” the statement said.

Hilton rose to fame in the early 2000s for his gossip blog, sounding off on celebrity drama. His commentary was often criticized as cyberbullying and labeled as “toxic.” However, Hilton attempted to turn a new leaf years later and embraced a gentler, softer version of himself.

“I’m aware of the fact there are going to be a lot of people with lingering resentment and a lot of skeptics,” he told the New York Times in a 2012 interview. “And that’s OK because I am not pretending to be perfect.”

title: ‘My Life With the Walter Boys’ Season 2 Recap: 7 Things to Remember Before Season 3
summary: Here’s what to remember before My Life with the Walter Boys returns for Season 3. Read a recap of Season 2.
story: The second season of “My Life with the Walter Boys” left viewers with two major cliffhangers. After a long year of waiting, fans are about to get the answers they’ve been craving when the hit Netflix series returns for Season 3 on Aug. 6.

Will Jackie (Nikki Rodriguez) and Alex (Ashby Gentry) be able to mend their relationship after she declared her love for Cole (Noah LaLonde)? Is George (Marc Blucas) going to survive his medical emergency? Viewers are ready to devour the 10 new episodes to find out.
Before Season 3 premieres, we’re recapping all the highlights from Season 2 so you can dive right in.
Jackie Returned to Colorado After Spending the Summer in New York City
At the end of Season 1, Jackie surprised the Walter family by leaving Colorado and returning to New York to live with her uncle, Richard (Alex Quijano).

Season 2 picked up with Jackie wrapping up a summer internship. It was a lonely couple of months for the teen since Richard was MIA and traveling a lot. Jackie no longer felt like she belonged in New York City, so she decided to attend boarding school in Vermont.

As Jackie’s legal guardian, Katherine (Sarah Rafferty) had to sign the paperwork for Jackie’s school transfer, and she wasn’t so sure that uprooting the teen once again was the right move. Luckily, Katherine visited Jackie in New York and convinced her to return to Colorado.

Back at the Walter ranch, Jackie got a lukewarm welcome. Several of the Walter siblings were upset that she left so suddenly a few months beforehand, but she quickly won them over and life began to return to normal.
Jackie’s Love Triangle with Alex and Cole Took a Brief Pause Then Got Messier Than Ever
At the end of Season 1, Jackie was dating Alex but also had undeniable chemistry with his brother Cole. In the Season 1 finale, Jackie and Cole ended up sharing a kiss, then she left town.
When she returned to Colorado at the beginning of Season 2, Jackie warned Cole that she hadn’t told Alex about their kiss and asked Cole to give her some space.

Alex was understandably frosty with Jackie when she returned, especially since she had blindsided him when she left town. Over time, he softened up and the two rekindled their romance. Due to their complicated history, they decided it was best to hide their relationship for a while. However, Cole caught the two kissing and  confronted Jackie in the season finale.

When Cole asked why Jackie and Alex got back together after breaking up, she defended their relationship. She also reminded Cole that they agreed to be just friends when she returned to town, despite the fact that they’d kissed. Cole responded by saying he was never just friends with Jackie.

Jackie explained that she was afraid of losing control with Cole since he makes her feel free. Cole responded by declaring his love for Jackie and she reciprocated his feelings. Unfortunately, Alex heard it all and he emerged from the darkness to ask Jackie if she really loves Cole.
Alex Became a Saddle Bronc Rider and Got a Riding Sponsorship

Much to the dismay of Katherine, Alex found a new hobby in Season 2: saddle bronc riding. His mom was understandably concerned that the sport is quite dangerous, but she arranged for him to get lessons with a rode trainer named Blake (Natalie Sharp). All of Alex’s hard work paid off since he ended up getting a sponsorship at the end of the season.
The Walters Faced Obstacles While Developing Their Ranch Expansion Project

In Season 1, the Walters came up with a plan to make their ranch more profitable with a new guest ranch business. In Season 2, Jackie’s uncle Richard was closely involved with the project as an investor.

Despite the family’s initial excitement about the ranch expansion, things started spiraling out of control as Richard became more involved. Will (Johnny Link) seemed to be eating up Richard’s ideas, even though his own father, George, was apprehensive about changing the ranch too much.

When many members of Silver Falls expressed concerns about the impact the ranch expansion would have on the community, the project was threatened. Soon enough, George and Katherine didn’t like the direction the project was going in and they wanted to back out. Richard had invested too much money into the project at this point, however, and threatened to cut George out of the project.

When George discovered that the ranch used to have a vineyard on it, he asked his friend to get in touch with a local winery. They agreed to lease the land to make immediate income and start paying back their investors. Will wasn’t happy but Richard was willing to listen to George’s idea.
George Had a Health Emergency

In the season finale, viewers were left with a cliffhanger in the last seconds when an ambulance showed up at the Walter house. Will also arrived and said, “It’s dad,” implying that his father had a health emergency.
Nathan Cheated on Skylar and They Broke Up
Nathan (Corey Fogelmanis) and Skylar (Jaylan Evans) were happily dating, but then Zach (Carson MacCormac), Skylar’s ex, came into the picture.
Zach started flirting heavily with Nathan and the two ended up kissing at a school dance. Skylar caught them and they broke up.

Zach and Nathan started dating and Nathan learned more about Zach’s history with Skylar. As it turns out, Skylar and Zach hooked up during their sophomore year, but Zach hadn’t publicly announced that he was gay yet. Skylar wanted to date someone who was openly gay so they went their separate ways.

Zach came out eventually, but by the time he did, Nathan and Skylar were already dating. So, Zach tried his best to lure Nathan away from Skylar to get Skylar’s attention, in the hopes that Skylar would ditch Nathan.

Eventually, Nathan and Zach broke up and Zach tried to get back with Skylar, but he had no interest. In the season finale, Nathan apologized to Skylar and they declared their love for each other. However, Skylar made it clear that he could no longer trust Nathan, even if he still loves him.
Two New Couples Emerged: Danny and Erin and Dylan and Kiley

Erin (Alisha Newton) previously dated Cole, but they had a pretty complicated relationship and he didn’t treat her very well. When Cole’s twin brother Danny (Connor Stanhope) starred in the school play with Erin in Season 1, sparks started to fly. The two kept in touch over summer break and started dating in Season 2.

Cole was pretty upset when he found out that his brother was dating his ex in secret, but eventually warmed up to their relationship. Danny and Erin seemed like the perfect match, but struggled to figure out how to maintain their relationship with college approaching.

Alex’s friend Kiley (Mya Lowe) found an unexpected new love interest in football player Dylan (Kolton Stewart). They had apparent chemistry throughout the season, but finally kissed in the season finale. Alex spotted them smooching and looked upset, despite the fact that he was happy with Jackie.

title: Karlie Kloss Loves to Answer This 1 Question: ‘What Does Karlie Have to Do With Tech?’
summary: Karlie Kloss talks to TODAY.com about her new children’s book, her passion for technology and why she thinks of Kode with Klossy as her “first baby.”
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com asks the burning questions our anchors couldn’t get to on-air.

Karlie Kloss has had quite a busy summer, from attending the star-studded wedding of a certain blonde pop singer to turning 34. Kloss is also reaching new heights with the release of a children’s book, “Spaghetti Code: A Story About Problem-Solving, Pasta, and the Power of Big Ideas.”

“Spaghetti Code” follows a girl named Kelly Kent who embarks on a quest to untangle the messy process of building a pasta machine to save her local Italian restaurant. In the endnotes, Kloss gives a message to readers: “For the builders, the breakers, and the curious creators — the world is waiting for you! — K.K.”

Following her TODAY segment on July 28, Kloss, who shares 3 children with Joshua Kushner, sat down with TODAY.com to talk more about Kode With Klossy, the free girls’ summer coding program she started nearly 11 years ago. She also shared how she’s combatted imposter syndrome and doubt, the relationships she’s maintained with her early scholars and why she considers the venture her “first baby.”
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

I could have never dreamed that Kode With Klossy would grow into what it has become, and this community of scholars around the world would be what it is, which is more than 12,000 incredible young people. We have a few 1000 more in programs this summer, and it’s surreal. I feel like I’ve really grown up with these young women. One of the scholars texted me this morning. I’ve known her since she’s 14 years old, and now she is just thriving in the world, she’s a leader, she’s an entrepreneur. She was like, “We met at camp 10 years ago on the day,” and I was like, “What a crazy full circle moment.” I now have a daughter as well. And so, to think that when she’s 10 years old, Kode With Klossy will be 20 years old, is just wild to me.

Oh my gosh, so much. And I think that’s the thing. Listen, I started working in my career at 15 years old. Just because you’re a young person doesn’t mean that you’re not extremely capable and curious. What we really aim to do is provide access to tools and skills that can build confidence in individuals. And that’s really what Kode With Klossy has always been about, and this book is sort of an opportunity to reach a younger audience with that same idea, of how we can sort of demystify something that can be really intimidating, coding and technology, but help young girls and young people see themselves in these spaces, and that I think is so important.

I think imposter syndrome is something that I’ve certainly experienced in different chapters of my life, but I think that’s part of why I started Kode With Klossy, and I think that’s part of why it has resonated. I am not an extremely educated person who’s worked in technology in this tech industry for my whole career. But that does not mean that I am not curious about these skills and tools. When I started this organization, people were definitely kind of confused. They were like, “What does Karlie have to do with tech?” But the truth is that I want everyone to realize that this is something we all can learn, and I think it’s important whether you want to work in the technology industry or not. It’s important to be informed how technology works as a consumer, as a citizen. So I think it’s important that people realize you don’t have to have a PhD in computer science to find value in understanding this.

We’ve had AI literacy for four years in our programs, and it’s been a central conversation all the way through. I really want young people to understand what is happening and understand these tools and not be intimidated by them, but to question it and to use it responsibly.

title: Al Roker Comes Face-to-Face with His ‘Twin’ on the TODAY Plaza: ‘That’s Freaky’
summary: Al Roker had to do a double take when he came face to face with his doppelgänger this morning.
story: Al Roker had to do a double take when he came face to face with his doppelgänger this morning.

The moment occurred Aug. 6 while the TODAY weatherman was visiting with fans on the TODAY Plaza. As he was doing a live segment, Al paused to speak with one special couple who brought a sign that caught his eye.
